title: Non-tuberculous mycobacteria (MOTT)
content:
NON-TUBERCULOUS MYCOBACTERIA (MOTT / NTM)

اللقب: أقارب السل الانتهازيون، لا ينتقلون بين البشر


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم (Name)
Mycobacteria other than tuberculosis (MOTT)، وتسمى non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM)
النوع (Type) بكتيريا من جنس المتفطرات (Mycobacterium) الشكل (Morphology / shape)
نفس شكل M. tuberculosis التصنيف (Classification)
حسب سرعة النمو وإنتاج الصبغ (staining)ة: بطيئة النمو وسريعة النمو
الموطن والأصل (Habitat & reservoir / origin)
البيئة: ماء الصنبور، ماء وحدات غسيل الكلى، التربة (soil)، الطيور (birds)، الأسماك
ملاحظة (Note)
قائمة الأنواع المهمة المسببة للمرض مقطوعة في الملف (تنتهي العبارة بـ «Species that are significant causes of disease are:» دون قائمة)


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
مرض رئوي لا يمكن تمييزه عن السل (ذُكر في مقدمة الملف)
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission) ليست سهلة الانتقال من شخص لآخر
الأسلحة (Weapons / virulence factors)
انتهازية: تسبب المرض عند ضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients) حين تكون بأعداد كبيرة
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
المرضى ضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients)
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
التعرف عليها غالبا بـ DNA probes. وإثبات أنها السبب يعتمد على تكرار عزلها. وقد تعطي اختبار سلين إيجابيا كاذبا بالتفاعل المتصالب

title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
content:
PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (الزائفة الزنجارية)

اللقب: صاحب القيح الأزرق ورائحة الفاكهة


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم العلمي (Scientific name)
Pseudomonas aeruginosa النوع (Type)
بكتيريا سالبة الجرام (Gram-negative bacteria) غير مخمّرة للسكر (non-fermentative)
الشكل (Morphology / shape) عصيات (bacilli) الحركة / الأبواغ (Motility / spores)
متحركة (motile) بسوط قطبي واحد، لا تكوّن أبواغا (non-spore-forming)
التنفس والنمو (Respiration & growth)
هوائية، مثلى عند 37°م وتنمو عند 42°م، احتياجاتها الغذائية بسيطة
الصبغات (Pigments)
تنتج صبغتين ذائبتين: pyoverdin (أصفر متألق) وpyocyanin (أزرق)، ويتحدان فيعطيان اللون الأخضر المميز للمستعمرات (colonies)
بصمة الزرع (Culture appearance)
تحلل الدم على آجار الدم (blood agar). على MacConkey: لا تخمّر اللاكتوز (مستعمرات (colonies) صفراء). للمستعمرات رائحة فاكهية
البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions)
لا تخمّر الكربوهيدرات، تنتج حمضا من الجلوكوز بالأكسدة (بلا غاز)، Oxidase موجب، Indole سالب
الموطن والأصل (Habitat & reservoir / origin)
التربة (soil) والماء (water) والنباتات وجلد بعض الأصحاء والحلق والبراز. في المستشفى مستودعاتها: المطهرات، أجهزة التنفس، الطعام، المغاسل، الصنابير، الممسحات

Pseudomonas Gram stain [api/images/wcmDlbZMnzB1/micro-pseudomonas-gram-stain.png]

Green pigment on nutrient agar [api/images/wj4tLOcf1W5h/micro-pseudomonas-green-pigment.png]

Hemolysis on blood agar [api/images/KbtI9rLvAM9K/micro-pseudomonas-hemolysis-blood-agar.png]

Non-lactose fermenter on MacConkey [api/images/NYVrd5aLqgVg/micro-pseudomonas-macconkey.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
التهاب رئوي (pneumonia) (مستشفوي)، وعدوى قيحية. هي رابع أكثر العوامل المستشفوية عزلا، وتسبب 10% من العدوى المكتسبة في المستشفى. ومنها «القيح الأزرق» (blue pus) بسبب pyocyanin، وعدواها غازية ومنتجة للسموم معا
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
من مستودعات المستشفى؛ تنتقل من مريض لآخر بأيدي العاملين، وبالتماس المباشر مع مستودع ملوث، وبابتلاع طعام وماء ملوثين. ويزداد حمل الجهاز الهضمي لها خلال 72 ساعة من دخول المستشفى
الأسلحة (Virulence factors)
الأهداب (pili)، كبسولة السكر المتعدد، السم الداخلي (endotoxin)، Exotoxin A، exo-enzyme S، elastase، alkaline protease، phospholipase C، leukocidin
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
ضحايا الحروق الشديدة، مرضى السرطان والإيدز (كبت المناعة). فهي ممرض انتهازي
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) غير مذكور في الملف
أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) غير مذكور في الملف
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
التعرف عليها بشكلها بجرام، عدم تخمير اللاكتوز، Oxidase موجب، النمو عند 42°م. ويفيد التألق تحت الأشعة فوق البنفسجية في التعرف المبكر على المستعمرات (colonies) وفي اقتراح وجودها في الجروح
مقاومتها (Antibiotic resistance)
تتحمل تراكيز عالية من الأملاح والأصباغ والمطهرات الضعيفة والمضادات. أسباب مقاومتها: بلازميدات المقاومة (R-factors)، تكوين biofilm يجعل الخلايا منيعة على الدواء، حاجز نفاذية يوفره LPS في الغشاء الخارجي، وانتشارها الواسع في الطبيعة فاكتسبت مقاومة لمضادات طبيعية
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment)
قليل من المضادات فعال: الفلوروكينولونات، الجنتاميسين (gentamicin)، الإيميبينيم
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
احتياطات مكافحة العدوى (infection control)، التقنية المعقمة، والعلاج الموضعي لجروح الحروق بمضادات الجراثيم

 * أدوية (Drugs): Aminoglycosides
 * أدوات تشخيص (Diagnostic tools): Bacterial identification tests • Special culture media

title: Serratia marcescens
content:
SERRATIA MARCESCENS

اللقب: المجرم ذو البصمة الحمراء


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم العلمي (Scientific name)
Serratia marcescens (أكثر أنواع الجنس شيوعا). تُذكر معها Citrobacter وEnterobacter
النوع (Type) بكتيريا سالبة الجرام (عصيات (bacilli))
الحركة / الأبواغ (Motility / spores)
متحركة (motile)، لا تكوّن أبواغا (non-spore-forming) البصمة
مستعمرات (colonies) حمراء الصبغ (staining)ة عند حرارة الغرفة، وتُستخدم لاختبار كفاءة المرشحات البكتيرية
الموطن والأصل (Habitat & reservoir / origin)
منتشرة في التربة (soil) والماء (water)، وموجودة طبيعيا في الجهاز التنفسي وبراز الإنسان (human) والحيوان

Serratia marcescens red colonies [api/images/B4SAlCcoOqip/micro-serratia-red-colonies.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
عدوى مستشفوية (nosocomial infection): التهاب رئوي (pneumonia) بالدرجة الأولى، التهاب مثانة، عدوى جروح، تسمم دم، التهاب شغاف القلب
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission) غير مذكور في الملف
الأسلحة (Weapons / virulence factors)
مقاومة (resistance) للمضادات الحيوية، لذلك العلاج صعب
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups) غير مذكور في الملف
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
الملف لا يفصّل غير المستعمرات (colonies) الحمراء عند حرارة الغرفة
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment) صعب بسبب مقاومتها الوقاية (Prevention)
غير مذكور في الملف

title: Streptococcus pneumoniae
content:
STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE (المكورات الرئوية)

اللقب: العميل الأول في الالتهاب الرئوي المكتسب من المجتمع


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم العلمي (Scientific name)
Streptococcus pneumoniae (Pneumococcus) النوع (Type)
بكتيريا موجبة الجرام (Gram-positive bacteria) الشكل (Morphology / shape)
مكورات (cocci) مستطيلة على شكل رأس الرمح (lancet-shaped)، أزواج أو سلاسل قصيرة، حجمها 0.5-1.2 ميكرومتر
المحفظة / الحركة / الأبواغ (Capsule / motility / spores)
لها محفظة (capsulated)، غير متحركة (non-motile)، لا تكوّن أبواغا (non-spore-forming)
التنفس والنمو (Respiration & growth)
هوائي أو لاهوائي اختياري (facultative anaerobe)، يحب ثاني أكسيد الكربون 5-10% (capnophilic)، 37°م، يحتاج أوساطا مدعمة
البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions)
Catalase سالب، يخمّر inulin، يعطي انحلال دم ألفا (alpha-hemolysis) على آجار الدم (blood agar)، حساس للأوبتوكين، يذوب في الصفراء (bile)
نقطة ضعف في بنيته (Structural weak point)
هشّ جدا: فيه إنزيم autolysin يهدم جدار الخلية نفسها، وهذا سبب ذوبانه في الصفراء (bile)
الأنماط المصلية (Serotypes)
90 نمطا حسب السكر المتعدد في المحفظة (capsule)؛ 23 نمطا منها تسبب أكثر من 90% من حالات الالتهاب الرئوي (pneumonia)
الموطن والأصل (Habitat & reservoir / origin)
يستعمر البلعوم والبلعوم الأنفي عند ثلث البالغين

Streptococcus pneumoniae in tissue [api/images/W2UiCUh1z4Fx/micro-spneumoniae-gram-smear.png]

Alpha-hemolytic colonies on blood agar [api/images/SLnpAU9cw2Zd/micro-spneumoniae-alpha-hemolysis.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
الالتهاب الرئوي الفصي (Lobar pneumonia) في كل الأعمار، وغالبا بعد عدوى فيروسية. يرتبط بالتهاب رئوي نزفي (hemorrhagic) وصديد في غشاء الجنب (empyema)
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
القطيرات التنفسية (respiratory droplets) الأسلحة (Virulence factors)
المحفظة (capsule) (تمنع البلع)؛ Protein adhesin (يثبّته في الاستعمار الأول)؛ Pneumolysin O (يدمر الخلايا المهدبة (ciliated cells))؛ Secretory IgA protease (يقطع الجسم المضاد IgA المفرز)
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
من أصيبوا بعدوى فيروسية تنفسية (مثل الإنفلونزا (influenza))، السكري (diabetes mellitus)، مرض الرئة المزمن (chronic lung disease)، خلل الطحال أو استئصاله
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) غير مذكور في الملف
أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms)
الملف يذكر فقط أنه يسبب التهابا رئويا فصيا؛ لا يفصّل الأعراض (symptoms)
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
العينة: البلغم (sputum). صبغة جرام (Gram stain) (تشخيصية). Latex agglutination لكشف سكر المحفظة (capsule). الزرع (culture) على آجار الدم (blood agar): انحلال ألفا، وللتفريق عن S. viridans: حساس للأوبتوكين، يذوب في الصفراء (bile)، يخمّر inulin
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment)
البنسلين (penicillin) هو الدواء المفضل. السيفالوسبورينات (cephalosporins) أو الإريثروميسين (erythromycin) لمن عنده حساسية من البنسلين. الفانكومايسين (vancomycin) للسلالات المقاومة (resistance) للبنسلين. وقد ظهرت سلالات متعددة المقاومة
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
التطعيم ضد المحفظة (capsule): لقاح (vaccine) سكر متعدد متعدد التكافؤ لضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients) وبعد استئصال الطحال (splenectomy)؛ ولقاح سكر متعدد مقترن بالبروتين (conjugated) للأطفال دون سنتين

 * أدوية (Drugs): Cephalosporins • Macrolides • Penicillins • Vancomycin
 * أدوات تشخيص (Diagnostic tools): Bacterial identification tests • Gram stain • Latex agglutination • Special culture media

title: Atypical Pathogens (Mycoplasma, Legionella, Chlamydia)
content:
ATYPICAL PATHOGENS (MYCOPLASMA, LEGIONELLA, CHLAMYDIA)


A. MYCOPLASMA PNEUMONIAE

The most common cause of primary atypical ("walking") pneumonia. It lacks a cell wall, so it is:

 1. Unaffected by antibiotics targeting cell-wall synthesis (penicillin and other beta-lactams).
 2. Pleomorphic (multiple shapes).
 3. Not stained by Gram, but by Giemsa.

Other characters: membrane contains sterols but cannot synthesize cholesterol; lacks many metabolic pathways (grows in chicken embryos); small (0.2-0.8 μm) so passes through bacterial filters; strict aerobe; P1 cyto-adhesin protein inhibits ciliary action in the bronchial tree.

 * Reservoir: human respiratory tract. Transmission: droplets, young age (5-15 years). Incubation: 2-3 weeks.
 * Symptoms: fever, headache, non-productive cough.
 * Diagnosis:
   * Early: clinical.
   * Direct: direct fluorescent antibody, PCR.
   * Culture: sputum or throat washings in special transport medium; "fried egg" colonies on serum-enriched agar after 3 weeks.
   * Serology: complement fixation (titer peaks 4-6 weeks; fourfold rise = recent infection); ELISA for IgM.
   * Nonspecific: cold agglutinins (IgM that agglutinate group O RBCs at 4°C but not 37°C); titer ≥ 125 suggests recent infection.


B. LEGIONELLA PNEUMOPHILA

 * Common in water sources; multiplies intracellularly in protozoa/amoebae.
 * Morphology: Gram-negative small bacilli, motile, non-spore forming.
 * Culture: aerobic, on buffered charcoal yeast extract (BCYE) agar; requires cysteine, so it does not grow on blood agar. 35-46°C for 10 days.
 * Source: domestic hot-water systems, fountains, cooling towers.
 * Transmission: droplets containing bacteria. No person-to-person transmission; Legionnaires' disease is not contagious.
 * Risk factors: immunosuppression, cigarette smoking, lung cancer, renal failure.
 * Pathogenesis: facultative intracellular pathogen; grows inside neutrophils and pulmonary macrophages; main host defense is cell-mediated immunity, which Legionella often escapes.
 * Incubation: about 2 weeks.
 * Diagnosis: DFA and PCR; culture; serology; urinary antigen detection.

Cellular pathogenesis of Legionella [api/images/QKtLq1ppqbF9/legionella-cellular-pathogenesis.png]


C. CHLAMYDIA (C. PNEUMONIAE, C. PSITTACI)

 * Small obligate intracellular parasites; contain DNA, RNA and ribosomes, so they are true bacteria.
 * Inner and outer membrane like Gram-negative bacteria, with lipopolysaccharide but no peptidoglycan. Stained by Giemsa, not Gram.
 * Cannot make their own ATP. Cultured in chick-embryo yolk sac or tissue culture.
 * Elementary body (EB): small (0.3-0.4 μm), infectious form with a rigid membrane; binds host cells.
 * Reticulate body (RB): non-infectious, metabolically active, replicating intracellular form with fragile membrane.
 * Cycle: EBs enter by endocytosis/phagocytosis → reorganize into RBs inside the endosome (prevent fusion with lysosomes) → replicate by binary fission → reorganize into EBs → cell lysis (C. psittaci) or extrusion by reverse endocytosis (C. pneumoniae).
 * C. pneumoniae: atypical ("walking") pneumonia; respiratory droplets.
 * Diagnosis: direct immunofluorescence and ELISA (antigen), PCR, tissue culture, serology (fourfold rise in complement fixation or ELISA; high IgM = recent infection).


كلمات مهمة | KEY WORDS

title: Viral Pneumonias (Influenza, Coronaviruses, COVID-19)
content:
VIRAL PNEUMONIAS (INFLUENZA, CORONAVIRUSES, COVID-19)


INFLUENZA VIRUSES

True influenza is an acute infectious disease caused by influenza viruses (family Orthomyxoviridae): spherical or oval, enveloped (-) RNA viruses with a segmented genome. Types A, B, C; all cause acute respiratory disease in humans. A and C infect multiple species; B almost only humans.

Structure

 * Single-stranded RNA in eight separate segments (RNP) with helical nucleoprotein.
 * Lipoprotein envelope carrying two spikes:
   * Neuraminidase (NA): viral penetration; releases virus from mucus.
   * Haemagglutinin (HA): attachment to host cell membrane (including RBCs).
 * The envelope makes the virion labile (heat, drying, detergents, solvents).
 * Replication occurs in the host cell nucleus.
 * Types classified by antigenicity of nucleocapsid and matrix proteins.

Influenza virus structure [api/images/ApVp4SfrqGvV/influenza-virus-structure.png]

Reassortment: mixing of genetic material of two viruses infecting the same cell (e.g., in a pig); responsible for major genetic shifts.

Antigenicity: type A subtypes are based on H (15 subtypes) and N (9 subtypes).

Antigenic shift Antigenic drift Change
Major: sudden replacement by a new strain with different HA and NA (reassortment), e.g., H1N1 to H3N2
Minor: random point mutations in viral RNA changing HA Occurs in Type A only
Influenza A and B Frequency Every 10-15 years Every 2-3 years

Pathogenesis

 * Reservoir: acute infection in man. Rapid transmission by droplets and fomites; epidemics. Incubation 1-3 days.
 * Virus binds HA receptors on respiratory epithelium; neuraminidase digests sialic acid, helps penetrate mucus and release new virions. Cell destruction occurs; viremia is rare.

Diagnosis (respiratory secretions): immunofluorescence; viral isolation in cell culture or eggs; serology by haemagglutination inhibition.

Vaccines give about 70% protection: "flu shot" (inactivated A and B) and nasal spray (live attenuated, LAIV; healthy people 5-49 years, non-pregnant).


CORONAVIRUSES AND SARS

 * Infect humans and animals (respiratory and enteric disease); cause one third of common colds and SARS.
 * Structure: the largest positive-strand RNA viruses; helical nucleocapsid and envelope with spike glycoproteins (corona = crown).

Coronavirus structure [api/images/P5YweFseMx1b/coronavirus-structure.png]

 * Transmission: aerosols and contaminated fomites; replication in respiratory epithelium (some also in GI epithelium). Incubation 3-10 days.
 * Symptoms like rhinovirus colds; diarrhea in some. Often asymptomatic with viral shedding.
 * Complications: middle ear infection, pneumonia in immunosuppressed, myocarditis.
 * Most infections undiagnosed and self-limiting; supportive treatment; no specific antivirals; immunity is short-lived.
 * SARS-CoV: appeared late 2002 in southern China; significant morbidity; respiratory distress causes death in 3-30%.
 * COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2): since mid-December 2019, Wuhan; most closely related to two bat SARS-like coronaviruses.
 * Lab: lymphopenia and raised aminotransferases (liver damage). Diagnosis by nucleic acid probes, viral isolation, rising antibody titer.
 * Infection control: isolate in negative-pressure rooms; health care workers wear respirators. No specific antivirals.
 * COVID-19 vaccine categories: live attenuated; inactivated; recombinant viral-vectored; protein subunit; virus-like particles; nucleic acid (DNA or mRNA).


كلمات مهمة | KEY WORDS

Term المعنى بالعربي Enveloped virus فيروس له غلاف دهني Segmented genome

إنزيم يساعد الفيروس على الخروج والنفاذ عبر المخاط Haemagglutinin (H)
بروتين يلصق الفيروس بالخلية Reassortment
اختلاط أجزاء المادة الوراثية بين فيروسين Antigenic shift
تغير كبير مفاجئ في الفيروس، يسبب أوبئة عالمية Antigenic drift
تغير صغير تدريجي بسبب طفرات Fomites أسطح وأدوات ملوثة Epidemic وباء
Incubation period الفترة من العدوى حتى ظهور الأعراض Viremia وجود الفيروس في الدم
Haemagglutination inhibition فحص مصلي لتشخيص الإنفلونزا Live attenuated vaccine
لقاح من فيروس حي مضعف Inactivated vaccine لقاح من فيروس ميت SARS

title: Adenovirus
content:
ADENOVIRUS (الفيروس الغدي)

اللقب: العدو الصامت في اللوزتين والغدد


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم (Name)
Adenovirus. سُمّي بذلك لأنه عُزل أول مرة من غدد (adenoids) الإنسان (human) اللوزية
النوع (Type) فيروس DNA مزدوج الشريط، غير مغلّف الشكل (Morphology / shape)
كبسيد عشريني الوجوه (icosahedral) باثني عشر رأسا تبرز منها ألياف penton؛ هو الفيروس الوحيد ذو الألياف البارزة المسؤولة عن الالتصاق والتراص الدموي والسمية
المستضدات (Antigens)
مستضد (antigen) مشترك للمجموعة: بروتين Hexon (مشترك بين كل الفيروسات الغدية ويستخدم في complement fixation والتألق المناعي). مستضد نوعي: بروتين Fiber (يحدد النمط بالتعادل أو تثبيط التراص)
الأنماط (Serotypes / types) أكثر من 52 نمطا مصليا عند الإنسان (human)
النمو (Growth)
ينمو بسهولة في مزارع الخلايا، يتضاعف في النواة ويكوّن أجساما متضمنة كبيرة داخل النواة
الصفات (Characteristics) متوطن عالميا، وقادر على إحداث عدوى صامتة مستمرة

Adenovirus [api/images/yeOOPjLlLGB0/micro-adenovirus.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
أمراض تنفسية، والتهاب المعدة والأمعاء، والتهاب الملتحمة (conjunctivitis)، والتهاب المثانة، والطفح. المتلازمات: عدوى بلا أعراض (symptoms)؛ التهاب بلعوم (pharyngitis) حاد مع حمى (سبب شائع لألم الحلق)؛ حمى البلعوم والملتحمة؛ التهاب رئوي (pneumonia) مدمر بعد الحصبة (measles) أو عند التعرض لجهاز تنفس صناعي (مستشفوي)؛ المرض التنفسي الحاد (ARD) وبائيا في المعسكرات العسكرية
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
الطريق البرازي الفموي، القطيرات التنفسية (respiratory droplets)، التماس من اليد إلى العين، والجنسي
الأسلحة والحيل (Weapons & tricks / virulence, evasion)
يصنع عدوى صامتة مستمرة في اللوزتين والغدد والأمعاء، وقد يستمر الإفراز أشهرا أو سنوات
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups) تُكتسب العدوى عادة في الطفولة
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) غير مذكور في الملف
أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms)
العقد اللمفية المحلية تتضخم وتؤلم. والعدوى عادة ذاتية الشفاء
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
مباشر: كشف المستضد (antigen) بـ ELISA والتألق المناعي، وكشف DNA الفيروس بـ PCR. عزل الفيروس في مزارع الخلايا وتحديد النمط بتثبيط التراص و/أو التعادل بأمصال نوعية. مصليا: ارتفاع العيار أربعة أضعاف يدل على عدوى حديثة
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment) مضادات الفيروسات غير فعالة
المناعة (Immunity) عدوى تعطي مناعة طويلة ضد النمط نفسه، وأجسام الأم واقية
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
ممارسات مكافحة العدوى (infection control) توقف الفاشيات المستشفوية؛ كلورة كافية لمنع فاشيات التهاب الملتحمة (conjunctivitis) في المسابح؛ كلورة مياه الشرب والصرف

ملفات القضية (Case files = lecture notes): Viral Pneumonias

title: Coronaviruses (SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2)
content:
CORONAVIRUSES (SARS-COV AND SARS-COV-2 / COVID-19)

اللقب: ذو التاج (corona = تاج)


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم (Name)
الفيروسات التاجية؛ ومنها SARS-CoV (المتلازمة التنفسية الحادة الوخيمة) وSARS-CoV-2 (مسبب COVID-19)
النوع (Type) فيروسات RNA موجبة الشريط، الأكبر بين فيروسات RNA موجبة الشريط
الشكل (Morphology / shape)
كبسيد نووي حلزوني وغلاف عليه نتوءات (glycoproteins) تشبه التاج
البروتينات (Proteins)
Spike (S)، Envelope (E)، Membrane (M)، Hemagglutinin-esterase (HE)، Nucleoprotein (N)، وRNA الجينومي
المضيف (Host) تصيب الإنسان (human) والحيوان وتسبب أمراضا تنفسية ومعوية
الأصل (Origin)
COVID-19 ظهر منذ منتصف ديسمبر 2019 في مدينة ووهان الصينية. ودراسة الجينوم تظهر أنه الأقرب إلى فيروسين تاجيين شبيهين بـ SARS من الخفافيش. وSARS ظهر أواخر 2002 في جنوب الصين وانتشر إلى أمريكا وأوروبا

Coronavirus structure [api/images/OZbIlzzM8ZQ4/micro-coronavirus-structure.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
الفيروسات التاجية العادية تسبب ثلث نزلات البرد (والـ Rhinovirus نصفها). وSARS-CoV بخلاف أقاربه يسبب عدوى ذات مرضية ووفيات عالية: الضائقة التنفسية تقتل 3-30% من الحالات. وCOVID-19 يسبب مرضا يشبه الالتهاب الرئوي (حمى (fever)، صعوبة تنفس، سعال (cough) جاف، آفات منتشرة في الرئتين)
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
الرذاذ المحمول جوا (aerosols) والأسطح الملوثة. التكاثر الرئيسي في ظهارة الجهاز التنفسي (respiratory epithelium)، وبعض الأنواع في ظهارة الجهاز الهضمي
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
المضاعفات (التهاب رئوي (pneumonia)) عند ضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients). والعدوى المتكررة شائعة لكثرة الأنماط المتداولة. لا مستودع حيواني للنزلات العادية
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) 3-10 أيام
أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms)
تشبه نزلة البرد، وقد يحدث إسهال (diarrhea). أغلب الحالات بلا أعراض (symptoms) مع إفراز للفيروس المعدي
المضاعفات (Complications)
التهاب الأذن الوسط (medium)ى، التهاب رئوي (pneumonia) عند ضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients)، التهاب عضلة القلب
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
أغلب العدوى لا تُشخّص وتشفى ذاتيا. في المختبر: نقص اللمفاويات (إصابة مباشرة للخلايا المناعية) وارتفاع إنزيمات الأمينو ترانسفيراز (تلف الكبد). التشخيص: كشف مباشر بمسابر الحمض النووي، عزل الفيروس وتنميته، أو المصل بارتفاع عيار الأجسام المضادة (antibodies). وللنزلات العادية: المجهر (microscopy) الإلكتروني المناعي والمصل
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment)
علاج داعم فقط. لا توجد أدوية مضادة نوعية. والمناعة قصيرة
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
مكافحة العدوى (infection control): يُعزل المصابون بـ SARS-CoV وCOVID-19 في غرف ضغط سلبي ويلبس العاملون الصحيون كمامات تنفسية (respirators). لقاح (vaccine)ات COVID-19 في ست فئات: فيروس حي مضعف، فيروس معطّل، لقاحات ناقلات فيروسية مؤتلفة، لقاحات وحدات بروتينية، جسيمات شبيهة بالفيروس (VLPs)، لقاحات الحمض النووي (DNA أو mRNA)

ملفات القضية (Case files = lecture notes): Viral Pneumonias

 * أعراض وعلامات (Symptoms & signs): Cough • Fever
 * أدوية (Drugs): COVID-19 vaccines

title: Influenza virus
content:
INFLUENZA VIRUS (فيروس الإنفلونزا)

اللقب: المتحول الذي يغيّر ملامحه كل بضع سنوات


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم العلمي (Scientific name)
فيروس الإنفلونزا (influenza)، من الفصيلة Orthomyxoviridae النوع (Type)
فيروس مغلّف (enveloped)، مادته الوراثية RNA سالب أحادي الشريط مجزأ
الأنواع (Subtypes)
A وB وC تسبب كلها مرضا تنفسيا حادا عند الإنسان (human). A وC تصيب أنواعا عدة، وB تصيب الإنسان تقريبا فقط
الشكل (Morphology / shape) كروي أو بيضاوي، وقد يكون طويلا خيطيا
المادة الوراثية (Genome)
RNA في ثمانية أجزاء منفصلة (RNP) مرتبطة ببروتين نووي حلزوني (NP)
الغلاف والنتوءات (Envelope & spikes)
غلاف دهني بروتيني عليه نتوءان: Neuraminidase (N): للاختراق وإطلاق الفيروس من المخاط. Haemagglutinin (H): للالتصاق بغشاء الخلية المضيفة بما فيها كريات الدم الحمراء
نقطة ضعف (Weak point)
الغلاف الدهني يجعله هشا: يتأثر بالحرارة والجفاف والمنظفات والمذيبات
التضاعف (Replication) داخل نواة الخلية المضيفة التصنيف (Classification)
A وB وC حسب مستضد (antigen) الكبسيد النووي وبروتين المصفوفة. وتُقسّم A إلى أنماط حسب H (15 نمطا) وN (9 أنماط)
الأصل والمستودع (Origin & reservoir)
المستودع (reservoir): عدوى حادة عند الإنسان (human). وإعادة التجميع تحدث مثلا في الخنزير

Influenza virus structure [api/images/sLm9UH8TNN7J/micro-influenza-virus.png]


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
الإنفلونزا: تتراوح من عدوى خفيفة أو بلا أعراض (symptoms) إلى شديدة جدا. والمضاعفات الرئوية: التهاب رئوي بفيروس الإنفلونزا نفسه، التهاب رئوي بكتيري (خاصة H. influenzae وS. aureus وS. pneumoniae)، وعدوى فيروسية إضافية مثل Adenovirus
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
القطيرات والأسطح الملوثة (fomites) بالاستنشاق إلى البلعوم أو الجهاز التنفسي السفلي؛ ينتشر بسرعة ويسبب أوبئة
الأسلحة والحيل (Weapons & tricks / virulence, evasion)
Reassortment: اختلاط المادة الوراثية لفيروسين يصيبان الخلية نفسها (مثلا في الخنزير)، وهو سبب التحول الكبير (Antigenic shift): يحدث في النوع A فقط كل 10-15 سنة، وهو استبدال مفاجئ بسلالة جديدة بـ H وN مختلفين (مثل HA1NA1 إلى HA3NA2) بلا مناعة سابقة. الانجراف (Antigenic drift): تغير صغير بطفرات نقطية في HA، يحدث في A وB كل 2-3 سنوات
آلية الهجوم (Mechanism of attack)
يرتبط بمستقبلات HA على الظهارة التنفسية، وNeuraminidase تهضم حمض السياليك وتساعد على اختراق المخاط وإطلاق الفيروسات الجديدة، فتتدمر الخلايا المخاطية. الفيروسيميا نادرة
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
المضاعفات الرئوية أكثر عند الصغار جدا وكبار السن (elderly) ومرضى القلب والرئة المزمنين. وينتشر بين تلاميذ المدارس والأماكن المزدحمة
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) قصيرة: 1-3 أيام
أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms)
حمى (fever)، ألم عضلات، صداع (headache)، التهاب بلعوم (pharyngitis)، سعال (cough). وعادة لا يوجد سيلان أنف (coryza) الذي يميز نزلات البرد
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
العينة: مفرزات تنفسية (شفط مباشر، غرغرة، غسل الأنف). مباشر: فحص سريع بالتألق المناعي. عزل الفيروس: تلقيح مزارع الخلايا أو البيض. مصليا: تثبيط التراص الدموي (haemagglutination inhibition)
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment)
Amantadine وrimantadine فعالان ضد النوع A فقط. Oseltamivir (Tamiflu) وzanamivir (Relenza) فعالان ضد A وB وقد يفيدان في إنفلونزا الطيور (birds). وفيروسات H5N1 مقاومة (resistance) عموما لـ amantadine وrimantadine
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
اللقاح (vaccine)ات تعطي نحو 70% حماية: (1) «حقنة الإنفلونزا (influenza)» لقاح معطّل من النوعين A وB، عضليا، للرضع فوق 6 أشهر؛ (2) بخاخ الأنف: لقاح حي مضعف (LAIV) للأصحاء 5-49 سنة وغير الحوامل؛ (3) لقاح اصطناعي قيد البحث. وقاية دوائية: Amantadine وrimantadine للنوع A فقط، وOseltamivir للنوعين A وB. والتعافي من العدوى يعطي مناعة جزئية ضد السلالة نفسها فقط

title: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)
content:
RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS (RSV)

اللقب: مكوّن الخلايا الملتحمة، العدو الأول للرضع


بطاقة الهوية | ID CARD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) الاسم العلمي (Scientific name)
الفيروس المخلوي التنفسي RSV، فصيلة Paramyxoviridae، جنس Pneumovirus النوع (Type)
فيروس مغلّف (enveloped virus)، RNA خطي أحادي الشريط سالب الاتجاه
الشكل (Morphology / shape) كروي أو متعدد الأشكال، 100-350 نانومتر
الغلاف (Envelope)
بروتينان سكريان: F (Fusion) لاندماج الفيروس بالخلايا واندماج الخلايا المصابة بالمجاورة مكونة syncytia (خلايا ملتحمة)؛ G للالتصاق بالخلايا المضيفة
ميزة تميزه (Distinguishing feature)
يفتقر إلى بروتينات H/N بخلاف باقي أفراد العائلة
مقاومته (Environmental resistance)
يبقى على الأسطح حتى 6 ساعات وعلى القفازات أقل من ساعتين؛ يفقد حيويته بسرعة مع دورات التجميد والذوبان والأحماض والمطهرات
الوبائيات (Epidemiology)
منتشر عالميا، وأغلب الأطفال (children) أصيبوا به قبل عمر 4 سنوات


السجل الجنائي | CRIMINAL RECORD

الحقل (Field) المعلومة (Information) التهمة (Charge / disease)
السبب الأكثر شيوعا لـ التهاب القصيبات (bronchiolitis)، وقد يتبعه التهاب رئوي (pneumonia) عند الأطفال (children) الأكبر والبالغين
طريقة الدخول (Route of entry / transmission)
قطيرات كبيرة، الأسطح الملوثة، الأيدي. يدخل عبر العينين والأنف
الأسلحة والحيل (Weapons & tricks / virulence, evasion)
يلتصق ببروتين G، وينتقل من خلية لأخرى فينتشر من الجهاز العلوي إلى السفلي. تنسد القصيبات بالحطام والمخاط ويحدث تضيق قصبي. وتسهم الاستجابة المناعية للمضيف في الأذى (السيتوكينات من الخلايا التائية)
الضحايا المفضلون (Preferred victims / risk groups)
الرضع (infants)، أطفال أمراض القلب الخلقية الزرقاء، ضعاف المناعة (immunocompromised patients)
فترة الحضانة (Incubation period) 4-8 أيام أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms)
التهاب أنف وبلعوم مع حمى (fever)، قد يتبعه التهاب قصيبات والتهاب رئوي (pneumonia). لا فيروسيميا. السعال (cough) قد يستمر 3 أسابيع. وأغلب الحالات بلا أعراض (symptoms)
طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis)
العينة: غسل الأنف أو شفطه أو المسحات، تُنقل على الثلج. مباشر: direct fluorescent antibody وELISA. عزل الفيروس: تأثير مرضي على الخلايا (CPE) خلال 2-5 أيام في مزارع مثل خلايا HeLa. المصل: الأجسام المعادلة غير مفيدة كثيرا
العقوبة (العلاج) (Punishment / treatment)
Ribavirin (نظير الغوانوزين) بالرذاذ، استخدم بفعالية محدودة المناعة (Immunity)
أجسام معادلة ضد بروتيني F وG وIgA، لكن المناعة الخلطية قصيرة فتتكرر العدوى
الوقاية (الحبس) (Prevention / containment)
غسل الأيدي والعزل (isolation) وتمريض المجموعات (cohort nursing). التمنيع الفعال لم يعد مستخدما. التمنيع السلبي: غلوبيولين مناعي مجمّع أو جسم وحيد النسيلة ضد البروتين F بحقن شهرية للرضع المعرضين خلال موسم RSV

ملفات القضية (Case files = lecture notes): Viral Pneumonias

 * أدوية (Drugs): Ribavirin
 * أدوات تشخيص (Diagnostic tools): Direct fluorescent antibody / Immunofluorescence • Serology

title: Microbe Shortcut
content:
MICROBE FILES: بطاقات الهوية والسجلات الجنائية

لكل ميكروب من ملفي Microbiology of Lower Respiratory System وBacterial Pneumonia (محاضرة قسم الميكروبيولوجي، جامعة 6 أكتوبر) ملاحظة فيها:

 1. بطاقة الهوية: الاسم والنوع والشكل والأصل والصبغة والزرع والبصمة الكيميائية، مع الصورة إن وجدت في الملف.
 2. السجل الجنائي: التهمة، طريقة الدخول، الأسلحة، الضحايا، أعراض الجريمة، طريقة الكشف، العقوبة، والوقاية.

كل معلومة مأخوذة من الملف. وإذا لم يذكر الملف شيئا كتبت «غير مذكور في الملف» ولم أكمل من عندي.

جدول واحد يجمع كل المشتبه بهم حسب أصل الالتهاب الرئوي، من ملف Bacterial Pneumonia وملف Microbiology of Lower Respiratory System.


حسب مكان الإصابة

مكتسب من المجتمع (Community-acquired) مكتسب من المستشفى (Nosocomial)

النمطي (Typical، الفصي Lobar) غير النمطي (Atypical، الخلالي Interstitial)

title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP)
content:
COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP)


RISK FACTORS

 * Aspiration: typically caused by anaerobes and Gram-negative organisms. Alcoholism and diabetes: pneumococcal pneumonia with bacteremia; anaerobes and mixed infections more common in alcoholics.
 * Oral steroids / immunosuppression: Legionella may be more common.
 * Cigarette smoking: the strongest independent risk factor for invasive pneumococcal disease in immunocompetent patients.
 * COPD: H. influenzae and Moraxella catarrhalis more common.
 * Nursing home residents: more CAP, with aspiration, Gram-negatives and anaerobes; H. influenzae is the commonest cause.

Pathogens implicated in community-acquired pneumonia [api/images/dc1D2whFpGWd/cap-pathogens-table.png]


CLINICAL FEATURES

 * Fever, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain.
 * In the elderly: non-specific; may present "off legs" or with confusion, without fever.
 * Examination: raised respiratory rate (may be the only sign in the elderly); tachycardia; localizing chest signs: reduced expansion on the affected side, signs of consolidation (reduced air entry, bronchial breathing, reduced percussion note, increased vocal resonance) and crackles.
 * A normal chest examination makes the diagnosis unlikely.


DIAGNOSIS OF CAP

 * Symptoms and signs of acute lower respiratory tract infection.
 * New focal chest signs.
 * New radiographic shadowing with no other explanation.
 * At least one systemic feature (sweating, fevers, aches, pains).
 * No other explanation for the illness.
 * Most helpful: fever, pleuritic pain, dyspnea, tachypnea, and chest signs.


SEVERITY ASSESSMENT

 * Wide range of severity. Early identification of high-risk patients guides admission and need for assisted ventilation.
 * CURB / CURB-65 predicts morbidity and mortality. Two or more adverse prognostic factors = high risk of death; manage as severe CAP.

Poor prognostic factors

 1.  Age ≥ 65
 2.  Coexisting disease: cardiac disease, diabetes, COPD, stroke
 3.  Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min (one of the most reliable predictors)
 4.  Confusion: abbreviated mental test score ≤ 8
 5.  Blood pressure: systolic ≤ 90 and/or diastolic ≤ 60 mmHg
 6.  Hypoxemia: PaO2 < 8 kPa and need for assisted ventilation
 7.  Urea ≥ 7 mmol/L
 8.  Albumin < 35 g/L
 9.  White cell count > 20 or < 4 ×1000/L
 10. Radiology: bilateral or multilobe involvement; progression of CXR changes in ICU
 11. Microbiology: positive blood culture

CURB-65 core factors: Confusion (new), Urea ≥ 7 mmol/L, Respiratory rate ≥ 30/min, Blood pressure (systolic ≤ 90 and/or diastolic ≤ 60), age ≥ 65.

Core factors present Mortality 4 83% 3 33% 2 23% 1 8% 0 2.4%

Low risk: age < 50, no coexisting disease, CURB score zero: may be suitable for home treatment.


INVESTIGATIONS

 * CXR: consolidation (most commonly lower lobes or multilobe); pleural effusion (more common in pneumococcal bacteremia).
 * CT chest: unlikely to add information; useful if diagnosis in doubt or the patient is severely ill and failing to respond, to exclude abscess, empyema, underlying malignancy or interstitial disease.
 * Blood tests: WBC > 15 ×1000 suggests bacterial (particularly pneumococcal) infection; > 20 or < 4 = severe infection. CRP is a more sensitive marker than WBC or temperature; serial measures help assess response.
 * Microbiology: guides antibiotic choice and limits resistance. In outpatients, pretreatment sputum Gram stain, culture and blood cultures are not recommended. They are crucial in hospital patients, especially severe CAP or patients treated empirically for MRSA or Pseudomonas, previously infected with them, or hospitalized and given IV antibiotics in the last 90 days. In severe CAP: urinary Legionella and pneumococcal antigen testing.
 * Oxygen saturation and ABG.
 * Sputum examination for TB if weight loss, persistent cough, night sweats, TB risk factors.
 * Pleural fluid (if present): microscopy, culture, sensitivity and pH to exclude empyema.
 * Viral and atypical pathogens only in severe CAP: serology on paired samples, and in those unresponsive to β-lactams.


MANAGEMENT

General

 * Oxygen if hypoxic (due to V/Q mismatch as blood flows through unventilated lung); aim saturation > 92%.
 * Fluids after assessing volume status (JVP, BP); encourage oral fluids; IV if depleted.
 * Monitor urine output.
 * Analgesia: paracetamol or NSAIDs (paracetamol is also antipyretic).
 * Nutrition.

Additional

 * Bronchoscopy (esp. after intubation in ITU): suction retained secretions causing lobar collapse, get cultures, exclude an endobronchial lesion.
 * Monitoring: temperature, respiratory rate, heart rate, BP, mental status, oxygen saturation.
 * Severe CAP on admission, or failure to respond with persisting hypoxia: transfer to HDU or ICU.

Antibiotics

 * Early administration improves outcome; give after taking samples.
 * Mostly empirical at diagnosis.
 * Duration (by consensus): 5-7 days non-severe uncomplicated; 10 days severe, microbiologically undefined; 14-21 days if Legionella, staphylococcal, or Gram-negative suspected.

Setting Preferred Alternative (intolerant or allergic) Community
Amoxicillin 500 mg-1 g tds PO
Erythromycin 500 mg qds PO or clarithromycin 500 mg bd PO
Hospital, not severe: oral
Amoxicillin 500 mg-1 g tds PO ± erythromycin 500 mg qds PO or clarithromycin 500 mg bd PO
Erythromycin or clarithromycin, or levofloxacin 500 mg od PO, or moxifloxacin 400 mg od
Hospital, not severe: IV needed
Ampicillin 500 mg qds IV or benzylpenicillin 1.2 g qds IV plus erythromycin 500 mg qds IV or clarithromycin 500 mg bd IV
Levofloxacin 500 mg od IV Hospital, severe
Co-amoxiclav 1.2 g tds IV or cefuroxime 1.5 g tds IV or cefotaxime 1 g tds IV or ceftriaxone 2 g od IV plus erythromycin 500 mg qds IV (or clarithromycin 500 mg bd IV)
Levofloxacin 500 mg bd IV plus benzylpenicillin 1.2 g qds IV

Recommended antibiotic treatment of specific causative organisms [api/images/OdvNIPJrTAMd/cap-recommended-antibiotics-by-pathogen.png]

Complications: see Nosocomial Pneumonia (complications of pneumonia) and Lung Abscess.

title: Nosocomial Pneumonia
content:
NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA

Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) and ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP).


DEFINITION

A new radiographic infiltrate with evidence of infection (fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis) with onset at least 48 hours after hospital admission.


PATHOPHYSIOLOGY

 * Hematogenous spread of organisms.
 * Aspiration of infected upper airway secretions.
 * Inhalation of bacteria from contaminated equipment.
 * Severely ill patients have impaired host defenses.
 * Altered gastric pH with illness and drugs: the GI tract is no longer sterile, giving a source of bacteria.
 * Cerebrovascular event and reduced conscious level are the major risk factors for aspiration.


RISK FACTORS

 * Age > 70
 * Chronic lung disease and/or other comorbidity (especially diabetes)
 * Reduced conscious level / cerebrovascular accident
 * Chest or abdominal surgery
 * Mechanical ventilation
 * Nasogastric feeding
 * Previous antibiotic exposure
 * Poor dental hygiene
 * Steroids and cytotoxic drugs

Causative organisms: see Nosocomial Pathogens.


CLINICAL FEATURES

Fever; productive cough; raised inflammatory parameters; new CXR infiltrate; deterioration in gas exchange. Diagnosis is often clinical; identifying the organism can be hard, especially if broad-spectrum antibiotics were already given.


INVESTIGATIONS

 * CXR: usually a non-specific infiltrate.
 * Culture blood, sputum and pleural fluid.
 * ABG for severity.
 * Renal and liver function tests (other organ dysfunction).
 * Serology is of little use.


MANAGEMENT

 * Antibiotics covering different organisms; intravenous, prolonged treatment usually needed.
 * Supportive: oxygen, fluids, ventilation if necessary.


COMPLICATIONS OF PNEUMONIA

 * Pulmonary: parapneumonic effusion (36-57%; most resolve spontaneously; thoracentesis recommended), empyema, abscess formation, ARDS.
 * Extrapulmonary: septicemia; metastatic infection (meningitis, endocarditis, septic arthritis); sequelae of the initial insult such as renal failure and myocardial infarction.

title: Nosocomial Pathogens (Klebsiella, Serratia, Pseudomonas)
content:
NOSOCOMIAL PATHOGENS (KLEBSIELLA, SERRATIA, PSEUDOMONAS)


KLEBSIELLA

Found in the respiratory, intestinal and urogenital tracts. ESBL-producing strains from the hospital environment cause serious infections.

 * Morphology: Gram-negative bacilli, non-motile (no H antigen), non-spore forming, capsulated, single or in pairs. The capsule is the virulence factor and produces mucoid colonies.
 * Culture: aerobic/facultative anaerobic; large moist colonies from the mucoid polysaccharide capsule (K antigen); lactose fermenters on MacConkey.
 * Biochemical: ferments all sugars with acid and gas; indole negative.
 * Pathogenesis: capsule (80 serotypes) impedes phagocytosis; endotoxin (fever, inflammation, shock); enzymes: cephalosporinases and ESBLs (resistance to cephalosporins).
 * Disease: community-acquired pneumonia, commonly in patients with chronic lung disease and diabetics; source endogenous or by droplets.
 * K. pneumoniae is intrinsically resistant to ampicillin. Antibiotic susceptibility testing is essential; identify ESBL producers.


CITROBACTER, ENTEROBACTER, SERRATIA

Motile Gram-negative bacilli, widely in soil and water; naturally in human respiratory tract and stool.

 * Serratia marcescens: red-pigmented colonies at room temperature. Nosocomial pneumonia, cystitis, wound infection, septicemia, endocarditis. Antimicrobial-resistant, so treatment is difficult.


PSEUDOMONAS AERUGINOSA (NON-FERMENTATIVE GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI)

 * Common in soil and water; opportunistic pathogen: severe burns, cancer, AIDS. Fourth most commonly isolated nosocomial pathogen (10% of hospital-acquired infections).
 * Morphology: Gram-negative bacilli, motile by a single polar flagellum, non-spore forming.
 * Culture: aerobic; 37°C, grows at 42°C. Two soluble pigments: pyoverdin (fluorescent yellow) and pyocyanin (blue), which together give the green colour. Hemolysis on blood agar; non-lactose fermenters on MacConkey; fruity odor.
 * Biochemical: oxidase positive, indole negative, acid from glucose by oxidation (no gas).
 * Virulence factors: pili, capsule, endotoxin, exotoxin A, exo-enzyme S, elastase, alkaline protease, phospholipase C, leukocidin.
 * Resistance: tolerates salts, dyes, weak antiseptics and many antibiotics. Mechanisms: R-factor plasmids, biofilm, outer-membrane LPS permeability barrier, wide distribution in nature.
 * Pathogenicity: pyogenic infections; "blue pus" (pyocyanin); invasive and toxigenic.
 * Diagnosis: Gram morphology, non-lactose fermenter, oxidase positive, growth at 42°C; fluorescence under UV light.
 * Treatment: few effective antibiotics: fluoroquinolones, gentamicin, imipenem.

title: Epidemiology and Microbiology of M. tuberculosis
content:
EPIDEMIOLOGY AND MICROBIOLOGY OF M. TUBERCULOSIS


EPIDEMIOLOGY

 * TB is the second leading infectious cause of death worldwide (after AIDS), killing around 2 million people per year, despite being potentially curable.
 * Highest incidence in sub-Saharan Africa; high-population countries in Asia (India, China, Pakistan, Indonesia) account for half the global burden.


MICROBIOLOGY

 * First cultured by Robert Koch in 1882.
 * Morphology: stained by Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN); acid-fast (resist decolourization with acid) because of mycolic acids in the cell wall. Thin, slightly curved bacilli, red serpentine cords on a blue background; non-motile, non-spore forming, non-capsulated.

Ziehl-Neelsen stain of M. tuberculosis [api/images/DMLDkc41BFuO/tb-ziehl-neelsen-stain.png]

 * Culture: obligate aerobes at 37°C, growth enhanced by 5-10% CO2; special nutrients.
   * Solid: Lowenstein-Jensen (L-J) medium: selective enriched; whole eggs (yolk), glycerol, asparagine, malachite green (makes it selective); solidified by heating.
   * Fluid: Middlebrook medium: synthetic enriched, could also be solid; made selective with antibiotics; used for susceptibility testing.
   * Growth is slow: generation time 18-24 h; primary isolation takes 2-8 weeks.
   * Bactec: radiolabelled palmitate; ¹⁴CO2 released is detected. MGIT: oxygen consumption makes a sensor fluoresce under UV. Both detect growth in 6-12 days.

Lowenstein-Jensen medium [api/images/smnaFMTxz8Uf/tb-lj-medium.png]

M. tuberculosis colonies on L-J medium [api/images/HryguNkWRSaO/tb-colonies-on-lj-medium.png]


RESISTANCE AND SENSITIVITY

 * Resistant to: drying (especially in sputum, for long periods); acids (3% HCl, 6% H2SO4) and alkalis (4% NaOH), both used to decontaminate samples; dyes such as malachite green; some antibacterials such as penicillin; darkness. This is due to the lipid cell wall.
 * Sensitive to: moist heat (60°C for 30 min, or 70°C for 3 min with sudden cooling; killed by pasteurization); disinfectants (glutaraldehyde, alcohol); drugs (rifampin, PAS, streptomycin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide); UV and sunlight.


CELL WALL

Thick, complex, lipid-rich waxy wall external to the peptidoglycan. It explains: impermeability to ordinary stains such as Gram; survival inside macrophages; resistance to complement lysis; induction of cell-mediated immunity; resistance to many antibiotics and to acids and alkalis.

Schematic diagram of the mycobacterial cell wall [api/images/YEjo3AIgyvTz/mycobacterial-cell-wall.png]


PATHOGENICITY

 * No exotoxins and no endotoxin in the wall. It prefers to infect macrophages and other reticulo-endothelial cells.
 * Pathogenicity is due to wall contents:
   1. Lipids (60% of the wall): mycolic acid, phosphatides, cord factor, waxes, sulfatides.
   2. Proteins: bound to wax; elicit tuberculin hypersensitivity (type IV).
   3. Polysaccharides: role uncertain; induce hypersensitivity reactions.

title: Pathogenesis
content:
PATHOGENESIS


TRANSMISSION

 1. Airborne: inhaling droplets < 5 μm that reach the alveoli. Droplets can stay airborne for hours.
 2. Ingestion of contaminated milk (M. bovis), or accidentally M. tuberculosis: intestinal infection.
 3. Direct inoculation through skin abrasion.


SEQUENCE OF DISEASE

 1. Infectious droplets lodge in the distal airways and are taken up by alveolar macrophages: either successful control or progression to primary progressive TB.
 2. A. Exudative lesions: acute inflammatory response, chiefly in the lungs at the initial site. About 2 weeks later bacilli travel by lymphatics to regional (hilar) lymph nodes, which enlarge.
 3. B. Granulomatous lesions: cell-mediated immunity (CMI) starts 2-10 weeks after infection. Infected macrophages produce IL-2, promoting Th1 cells and IFN-gamma. Th1 cells activate and attract more macrophages. Resistance to intracellular killing leads to a localized granuloma (tubercle), whose center undergoes caseation necrosis.
 4. Depending on immune status, a caseous tubercle may break into a bronchus, empty and form a cavity, or heal by fibrosis or calcification.

Ghon complex: the primary lung lesion plus the enlarged lymph nodes. Primary disease usually shows a single lesion in the middle or lower right lobe with enlarged draining nodes.


POST-PRIMARY TB

 * Develops in previously infected persons by endogenous reactivation of latent disease or exogenous re-infection. Most adult disease is reactivation, from latent TB lying dormant in the Ghon focus.
 * Usual site: a single cavitary lesion in the apical region. Lesions stay localized due to CMI; no lymph node enlargement. Delayed hypersensitivity promotes more rapid caseation.


LATENT VERSUS ACTIVE

Latent TB infection TB disease Frequency
~90% of those with positive tuberculin test ~10% Symptoms None; bacilli dormant
Malaise, low-grade fever, night sweats, fatigue, persistent cough, hemoptysis
Tuberculin test Positive Positive

title: Laboratory Diagnosis
content:
LABORATORY DIAGNOSIS

To diagnose TB one must detect and isolate a member of the M. tuberculosis complex from a clinical sample.


SPECIMENS

 * Pulmonary TB: 3 successive morning sputum samples; bronchoalveolar lavage or lung biopsy. In children or when sputum is not expectorated: gastric aspirate.
 * Decontamination and concentration: sputum and other non-sterile specimens are liquefied with N-acetyl-L-cysteine, decontaminated with NaOH (kills other bacteria and fungi), neutralized and concentrated by centrifugation.


A. DIRECT MICROSCOPY

Rapid, simple, sensitive. ZN stain: AFB appear as pink curved bacilli on a blue background. A positive smear allows early diagnosis and follow-up of therapy.


B. CULTURE

Definitive diagnosis. 37°C, 5-10% CO2, up to 8 weeks; Bactec and MGIT detect growth in 6-12 days.


C. PCR

Amplification of specific nucleic acid gives rapid diagnosis in 1-2 days but cannot replace culture and drug sensitivity testing.


D. IMMUNOLOGICAL TESTS

a. Tuberculin test (Mantoux)

 * Intradermal skin test detecting delayed hypersensitivity to previous exposure; detects latent infection.
 * 0.1 mL of PPD (5 tuberculin units) injected intradermally on the anterior forearm.
 * Presensitized Th1 cells secrete cytokines that recruit macrophages, giving a raised indurated area. Read after 48-72 hours; measure induration, not erythema, in millimetres.

Induration Positive in ≥ 5 mm
Previous TB disease; close contacts of an infectious case; HIV patients ≥ 10 mm
Persons in endemic areas; medical conditions such as diabetes; unvaccinated children < 4 years
≥ 15 mm Persons with no risk factors

(The "5-10-15 millimetre system".)

 * No reaction in persons not previously sensitized.
 * False negative: early primary infection (takes 2-10 weeks to turn positive); anergy (HIV, miliary TB, tuberculous meningitis, tumor); immunosuppressive agents.
 * False positive: cross-reaction with non-tuberculous mycobacteria (NTM); after BCG vaccination (lasts about 5 years).

Tuberculin test (Mantoux method) [api/images/w5Xq80nV3d7Y/tuberculin-test-mantoux.png]

b. QuantiFERON-Gold TB / interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs): measure IFN-gamma released by sensitized T lymphocytes in whole blood when exposed to TB antigens, detected by ELISA.

c. Antibodies from Lymphocyte Secretions (ALS) assay: based on antibody secreted by in-vivo activated plasma B cells in the blood for a short period in active TB rather than latent TB.

d. Transdermal patch: suggested method of detecting active TB: the patch contains antibodies recognizing a secreted mycobacterial protein; the skin reddens if detected.

title: Clinical Features and Investigations
content:
CLINICAL FEATURES AND INVESTIGATIONS


RISK FACTORS FOR ACTIVE TB

 1. Place and date of birth: Caucasian population: prevalence rises with age (M > F). Africans and Indian subcontinent: highest in middle age (M = F).
 2. HIV/AIDS
 3. Poverty and homelessness
 4. Prisons and military service
 5. Medical factors: diabetes, renal disease, malignancy, systemic chemotherapy, corticosteroids, new immunosuppressant drugs
 6. Smoking and vitamin D deficiency


SYMPTOMS

Most cases present with pulmonary disease:

 * Productive cough: the most commonly reported symptom is a persistent cough of 2 or more weeks.
 * Hemoptysis: more common with cavitary disease; up to two-thirds are smear-positive. Usually small; massive hemoptysis is rare, most common after destruction of a lobe with bronchiectasis.
 * Breathlessness
 * Systemic symptoms: weight loss, night sweats, malaise, fever
 * Chest pain


SIGNS

 * Signs of night fever, night sweats and weight loss.
 * Lymphadenopathy (particularly cervical).
 * Crackles; signs of pleural effusion; signs of consolidation in extensive disease.
 * Look for extrapulmonary disease: skin, joints, CNS, retina, vertebral bodies.
 * Physical findings are often non-specific. Bronchial breathing may indicate a cavity.
 * Chronic cough with sputum is not always present, even with smear-positive sputum.


COMPLICATIONS

 * Bronchiectasis
 * Lymph node enlargement compromising airway size
 * Pleural disease (primary progressive disease or reactivation): probably a delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction to mycobacterial antigens


INVESTIGATIONS

The diagnosis is usually bacteriological, in one of three ways:

 1. Sputum (or other sample: pus, CSF, urine; minimum three samples)
 2. Smear or culture
 3. Identification of tissue caseating granulomas

Imaging

 * CXR (usually first): upper lobe infiltrates with cavitation, possibly hilar or paratracheal lymphadenopathy; old TB shows fibrous scarring and calcification.
 * CT is more sensitive than CXR, especially for small areas.

Laboratory

 * Sputum ZN stain and culture: required for definitive diagnosis, and for sensitivity and resistance testing. Bronchoscopy with BAL if high clinical suspicion but non-productive cough or unhelpful sputum culture.
 * Nucleic acid amplification and DNA fingerprinting to confirm the mycobacterial type and drug susceptibility.
 * Tuberculin skin test: useful only if strongly positive (suggesting active disease) or negative; interpret with clinical picture, ethnic origin, exposure and BCG history.
 * Lymph node and pleural biopsies.

title: Management and Prevention
content:
MANAGEMENT AND PREVENTION


PRINCIPLES OF TREATMENT

 * Aims: cure without relapse, prevent transmission, and prevent emergence of drug resistance.
 * Long-term, multi-drug treatment. Never treat with a single drug.
 * Send material for bacteriological diagnosis before starting treatment.
 * Most patients can be treated as outpatients.


STANDARD REGIMEN (FULLY SENSITIVE ORGANISMS): 6 MONTHS

 * Initial 2-month phase: four drugs: rifampicin (R), isoniazid (H), pyrazinamide (Z), ethambutol (E) (or streptomycin).
 * Last 4 months: two drugs: rifampicin and isoniazid.
 * Extrapulmonary regimens may extend to 12-18 months (cerebral tuberculoma, meningitis, osteomyelitis).
 * Doses (pulmonary TB): rifampicin 10-20 mg/kg/day; isoniazid 5 mg/kg/day; ethambutol 15-25 mg/kg/day; pyrazinamide 15-30 mg/kg/day for 2 months, then isoniazid and rifampicin for 4 months.


DRUG-RESISTANT TB

 * MDR-TB: resistant to two or more first-line agents, usually isoniazid and rifampicin.
 * XDR-TB: resistant to at least three classes of second-line drugs.


PREVENTION

BCG vaccination is obligatory in the Egyptian vaccination program, targeting all infants during the first month of life.

Drug details: Anti-TB Drugs.

title: Anti-TB Drugs
content:
ANTI-TB DRUGS


I. FIRST-LINE DRUGS

Drug Pharmacology Side effects and interactions Isoniazid (INH)
Oral; absorption decreased by aluminum antacids; distributed to all body fluids; metabolized by acetylation (rapid is dominant, or slow). Bactericidal for rapidly dividing organisms, bacteriostatic in the stationary phase. Inhibits mycolic acid synthesis (cell wall); acts intra- and extracellularly
Peripheral neuritis (esp. slow acetylators; competition with pyridoxine); allergy (rash, fever, blood dyscrasias, hepatitis); hemolysis in G-6-PD deficiency. Inhibits metabolism of phenytoin
Rifampicin
Oral; penetrates macrophages; liver metabolism; excreted in urine, sweat, stools, saliva. Bactericidal; inhibits DNA-dependent RNA polymerase; intra- and extracellular. Active against TB, M. leprae, meningococci, H. influenzae, Gram-positives
Impaired liver function and jaundice, gut upset; allergy (fever, rash, thrombocytopenia); flu-like symptoms; ataxia, confusion; red-orange discoloration of urine, saliva, sputum. title: Epidemiology and Etiology
content:
EPIDEMIOLOGY AND ETIOLOGY


EPIDEMIOLOGY

 * The most common malignant tumor worldwide, with 1.3 million deaths annually. The third most common cause of death after heart disease and pneumonia.
 * Mortality has leveled off in men but continues to rise in women, and now causes more cancer deaths in women than any other tumor, including breast cancer.


ETIOLOGY

 * Cigarette smoking: the association overshadows any other etiological factor.
   * 90% of lung cancers occur in active smokers or recent ex-smokers.
   * Women show higher susceptibility to tobacco carcinogens than men.
   * Squamous and small cell cancers have the strongest association with tobacco.
 * Passive smoking increases the risk by a factor of 1.5.
 * Urban versus rural: higher incidence in urban areas even after allowing for smoking.
 * Occupational factors: asbestos; also arsenic, chromium, iron oxide, petroleum products and oils, coal tar, products of coal combustion, radiation. Occupational tumors are mostly adenocarcinomas and less related to smoking.
 * Other carcinogens: arsenic, chromium, uranium, nickel, vinyl chloride, asbestos.


MOLECULAR PATHOGENESIS

 * The cancer arises by stepwise accumulation of genetic abnormalities, transforming normal bronchial epithelium into neoplastic tissue.
 * The molecular sequence parallels histological progression: inactivation of the suppressor gene on 3p is a very early event; TP53 mutation or K-RAS oncogene activation occurs relatively late.

title: Pathology and Histological Types
content:
PATHOLOGY AND HISTOLOGICAL TYPES


HISTOLOGICAL TYPES

The 4 major types: squamous, adenocarcinoma, large cell undifferentiated, small cell.

Five main histologic types: (i) squamous cell (epidermoid), (ii) small cell, (iii) adenocarcinoma (including bronchioloalveolar), (iv) large cell, (v) combined squamous and adenocarcinoma (adenosquamous).

Over the last 25 years small cell carcinoma incidence has declined while adenocarcinoma has risen and surpassed squamous cell carcinoma as the most frequent subtype.


THERAPEUTIC CLASSIFICATION

Group Frequency Includes Small cell carcinoma (SCC) 20-25%
Non-small cell carcinoma (NSCC) 70-75% Squamous, adenocarcinoma, large cell
Combined / mixed 5-10%


GROSS TYPES

 1. Hilar (central) type: most commonly arises in the main bronchus or segmental branches in the hilar parts, more often on the right.
 2. Peripheral type: a small proportion, chiefly adenocarcinomas including bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, arise from a small peripheral bronchiole.


SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA

 * Historically the most common type; more common in men, with a history of smoking.
 * Arises in the main bronchi and spreads to hilar nodes. Larger lesions may undergo central necrosis and cavitation.
 * Develops through squamous metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma; changes can be detected by cytology of sputum, bronchial lavage or brushings.
 * As it enlarges it may occlude major bronchi, causing distal atelectasis and infection, and invades surrounding lung.
 * Histology: well to poorly differentiated.


ADENOCARCINOMA

 * The most common bronchogenic carcinoma in women.
 * Usually peripheral, often arising in relation to a peripheral lung scar. Weak association with smoking. Grows slowly and forms a small mass but metastasizes widely at an early stage.
 * Histology: acinar, papillary and solid forms; solid type may need demonstration of intracellular mucin.
 * Bronchoalveolar carcinoma (grows along preexisting alveolar structures, preserving alveolar architecture) belongs here.


LARGE CELL CARCINOMA

 * Cells too anaplastic to be placed in either of the former types; many giant cancer cells, some spindle-shaped.
 * Poor prognosis; spreads to distant sites early.


SMALL CELL CARCINOMA

 * Strongly related to cigarette smoking; highly malignant.
 * Arises from major bronchi and extends to lung substance and hilar and mediastinal nodes.
 * Cells round to fusiform, scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin; about twice the size of a resting lymphocyte.
 * Necrosis almost always present. Cells are fragile, with crush artifacts in small samples; nuclear molding seen on cytology.
 * Express neuroendocrine markers (derived from lung neuroendocrine cells).


SPREAD

Direct invasion of adjoining structures, or lymphatic and hematogenous spread. Extension of an apical tumor into the thoracic cage may involve the brachial plexus and sympathetic chain, causing pain and sensory disturbance: Pancoast's syndrome.

title: Clinical Features
content:
CLINICAL FEATURES


LOCAL SYMPTOMS

 * May have no symptoms.
 * Cough.
 * Chest pain and discomfort, often described as fullness and pressure; may be pleuritic if the pleura or ribs are invaded.
 * Hemoptysis.
 * Recurrent chest infection.
 * Malaise, weight loss.
 * Dyspnea and shortness of breath.
 * Clubbing.


LOCAL AND REGIONAL SPREAD

 * Enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; signs of a pleural effusion.
 * Pancoast's tumor: apical carcinoma erodes ribs and involves the lower brachial plexus (C8, T1, T2): severe shoulder pain radiating down the inner arm. Involvement of the sympathetic ganglion gives Horner's syndrome: unilateral ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis with unilateral facial flushing.
 * Hilar tumors may involve the left recurrent laryngeal nerve: unilateral vocal cord paresis, hoarseness and a bovine cough.
 * Direct invasion of the phrenic nerve: paralysis of the ipsilateral hemidiaphragm.
 * Esophagus: progressive dysphagia. Pericardium: pericardial effusion and malignant dysrhythmias.
 * Superior vena cava (SVC) obstruction: early-morning headache, facial congestion, oedema of the upper limbs, distended jugular veins and chest veins forming a collateral circulation.


METASTATIC COMPLICATIONS

 * Bone metastases common: severe pain and pathological fractures.
 * Frequent liver involvement.
 * Brain deposits: personality change, epilepsy, or focal neurological lesion.
 * Spinal cord compression: not uncommon; needs urgent treatment.
 * Adrenal deposits: common at postmortem but often asymptomatic.


PARANEOPLASTIC SYNDROMES

Endocrine (usually small-cell carcinoma)

 * Ectopic ACTH syndrome
 * SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion)
 * Hypercalcemia (usually squamous cell carcinoma)
 * Rarer: hypoglycemia, thyrotoxicosis, gynecomastia

Neurological

 * Encephalopathies, including subacute cerebellar degeneration
 * Peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy
 * Muscular disorders: polymyopathy, myasthenic syndrome

Vascular and hematological: DVT and thrombophlebitis.

title: Investigations and Treatment
content:
INVESTIGATIONS AND TREATMENT


INVESTIGATIONS

 * Radiology: chest X-ray and CT.
 * Fiberoptic bronchoscopy: obtains biopsy and cytological specimens, and shows whether the tumor is operable (e.g., for pneumonectomy).
 * Percutaneous aspiration and biopsy: peripheral lesions cannot be seen by bronchoscopy; sampled through the chest wall under CT guidance.
 * Other: full blood count (anemia) and biochemistry (liver involvement, hypercalcemia, hyponatremia).


TREATMENT

Best planned by a multidisciplinary team.

 * Staging: TNM classification for non-small cell cancer. Small-cell cancer is treated according to whether it is limited or extensive.
 * Modalities:
   * Surgery: lobectomy, pneumonectomy
   * Chemotherapy and/or radiotherapy
   * Combined surgery with chemotherapy or radiotherapy
   * Palliative therapy must not be ignored: relieves severe pain, cough and hypoxia, aiming for a symptom-free and as active as possible remaining life.

title: Clinical Picture and Radiology
content:
CLINICAL PICTURE AND RADIOLOGY


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * Small effusions are often symptomless. Even very large effusions, if they accumulate slowly, may cause little or no discomfort.
 * The usual symptom of a large effusion is shortness of breath, often with a dull ache on the affected side.
 * If due to inflammatory disease, it often starts with pleuritic pain that may be relieved as fluid accumulates.
 * Recurrent dry cough is frequent, especially if the fluid accumulated quickly.
 * Findings depend on the size and site. Large effusions lie in the dependent part of the pleural space, so there are diminished movements, dull percussion notes, and distant or absent breath sounds there.
 * Large effusions displace the mediastinum to the opposite side, unless there is underlying pulmonary collapse or pleural fibrosis.


RADIOLOGICAL FEATURES

 * Detected on X-ray when 300 mL or more of fluid is present, and clinically when 500 mL or more.
 * Appearances range from obliteration of the costophrenic angle to dense homogeneous shadows occupying part or all of the hemithorax.
 * Pleural effusion is a common presentation of a wide range of diseases.

title: Diagnosis: Transudate versus Exudate
content:
DIAGNOSIS: TRANSUDATE VERSUS EXUDATE


DIAGNOSIS

By pleural aspiration (with ultrasound guidance if small). The fluid may be a transudate or an exudate. Pleural aspiration (thoracentesis) may be diagnostic and/or therapeutic; a breathless patient may benefit from removal of a larger volume.

After a diagnostic tap

 * Note the appearance of the fluid.
 * Biochemistry: sterile pot for protein and LDH.
 * Cytology: fresh 20 mL sample for malignant cells and differential cell count.
 * Microbiology: sterile pot and blood culture bottles for Gram stain, culture, and AFB stain and culture.
 * Analysis for pH.


TRANSUDATE

 * Can be bilateral, often larger on the right.
 * Protein < 30 g/L and LDH < 200 IU/L and/or fluid-to-serum ratio < 0.6.
 * Causes: heart failure, hypoproteinemia (e.g., nephrotic syndrome), constrictive pericarditis, hypothyroidism.


EXUDATE

 * Protein > 30 g/L and LDH > 200 IU/L.
 * Causes: bacterial pneumonia (common); carcinoma of the bronchus and pulmonary infarction (fluid may be blood-stained, common); tuberculosis; connective tissue disease; mesothelioma.


LIGHT'S CRITERIA

An effusion is exudative if it meets one of the following (very sensitive):

 * Pleural fluid protein / serum protein ratio > 0.5
 * Pleural fluid LDH / serum LDH ratio > 0.6
 * Pleural fluid LDH > two-thirds of the upper limit of normal serum LDH

title: Chylothorax and Empyema
content:
CHYLOTHORAX AND EMPYEMA


CHYLOTHORAX

Accumulation of lymph in the pleural space, usually from leakage of the thoracic duct following trauma or infiltration by carcinoma.


EMPYEMA

Pus within the pleural cavity.

 * Usually arises from bacterial spread from severe pneumonia or after rupture of a lung abscess into the pleural space.
 * Typically the cavity is infected with anaerobic organisms; the patient is severely ill with high fever and neutrophil granulocytosis.

Investigations

 * Bacteriological investigation of lung abscess and empyema is best done on specimens obtained by transtracheal aspiration, bronchoscopy, or percutaneous transthoracic aspiration with ultrasound or CT guidance.
 * Bronchoscopy helps to exclude carcinomas and foreign bodies.

Treatment

 * Appropriate antibiotics for up to 6 weeks, covering both aerobic and anaerobic organisms.
 * Prompt insertion of an intercostal drain under ultrasound or CT guidance.
 * If drainage is inadequate: surgery to clear the cavity and insertion of a large-bore tube.

See the surgical details in Empyema of the Pleural Cavity. Related: Lung Abscess.

title: Definition, Causes and Types
content:
DEFINITION, CAUSES AND TYPES


DEFINITION

 * The respiratory system has a gas-exchanging organ (the lungs) and a ventilatory pump (respiratory muscles and thorax). Either or both can fail.
 * Respiratory failure occurs when pulmonary gas exchange is impaired enough to cause hypoxemia with or without hypercarbia.
 * In practical terms: PaO2 < 8 kPa (60 mmHg) or PaCO2 > 7 kPa (55 mmHg).


TYPES

Type I ("hypoxemic") Type II ("ventilatory failure") Blood gases
PaO2 low, PaCO2 normal or low PaO2 low, PaCO2 high Mechanism
Diseases that damage lung tissue; right-to-left shunts or V/Q mismatch
Alveolar ventilation insufficient to excrete the CO2 produced: reduced ventilatory effort, inability to overcome increased resistance, failure to compensate for increased dead space and/or CO2 production
Causes Pulmonary oedema, pneumonia, pneumothorax, chronic lung fibrosis
COPD (most common); chest-wall deformities; respiratory muscle weakness (e.g., Guillain-Barré syndrome); depression of the respiratory center (e.g., overdose); obese hypoventilation syndrome


ACUTE VERSUS CHRONIC

 * Acute: develops within minutes or hours in patients with no or minor pre-existing respiratory disease.
 * Acute on chronic: acute deterioration in someone with pre-existing respiratory failure.
 * Chronic: develops over several days or longer in patients with existing respiratory disease.


CAUSES OF RESPIRATORY FAILURE (TABLE IN THE HANDOUT)

Acute Chronic Type 1
Acute pulmonary oedema; pneumonia; acute lung injury / ARDS; pneumothorax; severe acute asthma
Interstitial lung diseases (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, sarcoidosis and others); lymphangitic carcinomatosis; chronic pulmonary emboli; chronic heart failure
Type 2
Acute exacerbations of COPD; tension pneumothorax; Guillain-Barré syndrome; myasthenia gravis; laryngeal oedema; inhaled foreign body
COPD; obesity hypoventilation syndrome; motor neuron disease and other neuromuscular disorders

title: Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment
content:
MONITORING, INVESTIGATIONS AND TREATMENT


CLINICAL MONITORING OF RESPIRATORY DISTRESS

 * Cyanosis: bluish coloration of mucous membranes and nail beds
 * Use of accessory muscles of respiration
 * Intercostal muscle recession
 * Tachypnea, tachycardia, sweating
 * Inability to speak, unwillingness to lie flat
 * Agitation, restlessness, diminished conscious level


INVESTIGATIONS

 * Arterial blood gas (ABG): guides oxygen therapy and objectively assesses severity. The sample must be adequately anticoagulated and analyzed immediately (or the syringe immersed in iced water).
 * Chest X-ray: pneumonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, ILD.
 * ECG and echocardiography.
 * Complete blood count: leukocytosis.
 * Cardiac markers: troponin.


TREATMENT

 * A B C D E: maintain adequate oxygen delivery; mechanical ventilation if indicated.
 * Treat the cause: infection, heart failure and pulmonary edema, pneumothorax, etc.
 * Noninvasive ventilation (NIV): only in conscious patients with spontaneous breathing. Improves respiratory acidosis, reduces respiratory rate and dyspnea, reduces complications and hospital stay, decreases mortality and need for intubation.
 * Invasive mechanical ventilation after endotracheal intubation: in unconscious and comatose patients with apnea.

Mechanical ventilation [api/images/wiHmPYRGH2Nm/mechanical-ventilation.png]

title: ARDS
content:
ACUTE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (ARDS)


DEFINITION

Essentially: acute, persistent lung inflammation with increased vascular permeability; bilateral and extensive infiltrates on CXR; very poor oxygenation; not due to clinical left ventricular failure. It results in acute respiratory failure.


PATHOPHYSIOLOGY

 * Inflammatory damage to the alveoli, by locally produced pro-inflammatory mediators or remotely produced ones arriving through the pulmonary artery.
 * Increased pulmonary capillary permeability lets fluid and protein leak into the alveolar spaces.
 * Alveolar surfactant is diluted and loses its stabilizing effect: diffuse alveolar collapse, stiff lungs, reduced lung volume and compliance.
 * ABG: respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia that does not respond to increased % of O2.
 * CXR: interstitial edema.


CAUSES

 * Sepsis / pneumonia, especially COVID-19 pneumonia
 * Gastric aspiration (even on a proton pump inhibitor, showing that low pH is not the only damaging component)
 * Trauma / burns via sepsis, lung trauma, smoke inhalation, fat emboli, and possibly direct effects of large amounts of necrotic tissue


PATHOGENESIS

In both neonatal and adult ARDS, alveolocapillary wall damage is triggered by the above factors, and the final pathologic consequence, formation of hyaline membrane, is similar.

Sequence of events leading to hyaline membrane formation in adult ARDS [api/images/ZwKdyRY5tdyf/ards-hyaline-membrane-pathogenesis.png]


MORPHOLOGY

Gross: lungs normal in size; stiff, congested, heavy and airless, so they sink in water.

Microscopic

 1. Collapsed alveoli (atelectasis) alternating with dilated alveoli.
 2. Necrosis of alveolar epithelial cells and characteristic eosinophilic hyaline membranes lining the respiratory bronchioles.
 3. Interstitial and intra-alveolar oedema, congestion and hemorrhages.
 4. With time, compensatory proliferation of pneumocytes.
 5. In the organizing stage, interstitial fibrosis.


CLINICAL FEATURES

Consider ARDS in any patient with a predisposing risk factor who develops severe hypoxemia, stiff lungs, and widespread diffuse infiltrates on CXR; CT shows diffuse alveolar infiltrates and air bronchograms.


MANAGEMENT

 * Treat the precipitating cause.
 * Best supportive care with adequate oxygenation; watch for nosocomial infections.
 * Mechanical ventilation.

title: Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures
content:
AETIOLOGY AND SIMPLE RIB FRACTURES


AETIOLOGY

 1. Direct trauma: usually blunt (blow, car accident, fall from height). One or multiple ribs fractured at the site of impact; the broken ends are driven inwards, causing pleural and lung injury.
 2. Indirect trauma: antero-posterior chest compression, e.g., in bursts.
 3. Muscular strain: violent cough or lifting a heavy weight may fracture the anterior segment of a rib in old people with senile osteoporosis.

Types: (1) simple rib fracture, (2) flail chest.

Broken ribs [api/images/Ec6FZbOO5Xm0/rib-fractures.png]


SIMPLE RIB FRACTURES

Usually caused by direct chest trauma.

Symptoms

 * History of chest trauma; localized pain at the fracture site.
 * In multiple fractures, severe pain with limited respiratory expansion causes dyspnea; dyspnea may be severe if complicated by hemothorax or pneumothorax.
 * Symptoms of associated injuries elsewhere.

General examination: dyspnea; signs of shock (neurogenic, hypovolemic); search for associated injuries (head, abdomen, limbs).

Chest examination

Findings Inspection Localized ecchymosis; external wound may be present
Palpation
Localized tenderness and crepitus at the fracture; normal TVF in uncomplicated cases; no tracheal shift
Auscultation Equal air entry on both sides in uncomplicated cases

Complications: hemothorax, pneumothorax, lung contusion; limited respiratory movement leading to atelectasis and chest infection.

Investigations: plain chest X-ray (number and sites of fractures; detects hemo- or pneumothorax); abdominal ultrasound and CT for suspected injuries elsewhere.

Treatment

 1. Manage shock if present (analgesics, IV fluids).
 2. Pain relief with analgesics to permit proper respiratory movement.
 3. Intercostal nerve block for persistent pain (anesthetic injected in the intercostal spaces above and below the fractured rib).
 4. Elastic corset, useful especially in the elderly.

title: Flail Chest
content:
FLAIL CHEST

Occurs when 4 or more ribs are fractured at 2 points on one side of the chest wall. Usually caused by crush injury, as in a severe car accident.

Flail chest [api/images/muLLMWExW6Sr/flail-chest.png]


PATHOPHYSIOLOGY

 * Paradoxical movement: the integrity of the chest wall is lost; the flail segment moves inward during inspiration and outward during expiration. When it retracts inward it can injure the lung. This limits the ability to create negative intrathoracic pressure, interfering with respiratory efficiency: hypoxia and CO2 retention.
 * Pendulum respiration: air is rebreathed between the healthy and affected lungs; oscillation of gases raises blood CO2 tension, depresses the respiratory center, and may end in respiratory failure.
 * Mediastinal flutter: side-to-side movement of the mediastinum during respiration, which impedes heart action. Efficient negative intrathoracic pressure cannot be created on the normal side, so venous return decreases and shock worsens, ending in circulatory failure.

Paradoxical movement of the flail segment [api/images/TitUr1Hha0sk/flail-chest-paradoxical-movement.png]


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * Symptoms: history of severe chest trauma; marked chest pain; shortness of breath.
 * General: signs of shock; pallor, cyanosis; associated injuries.
 * Inspection: ecchymosis; limited chest expansion on the affected side; paradoxical movement may be evident.
 * Palpation: tenderness and crepitus; decreased TVF.
 * Auscultation: decreased air entry on the affected side.

Complications: respiratory failure, hemothorax, pneumothorax.


INVESTIGATIONS

 * Plain X-ray: multiple fractured ribs at 2 sites on the same side; may show hemo- or pneumothorax.
 * ABG: decreased PO2 and increased PCO2; pH decreased in severe cases; respiratory failure may be evident.


TREATMENT

 1. Small flail segment: external immobilization with adhesive plaster.
 2. Severe cases with marked paradoxical movement: the best is an endotracheal tube and intermittent positive pressure ventilation (IPPV), which gives internal stabilization of the flail segment.
 3. Uncontrolled cases: internal fixation with stainless steel wire,
 4. splint or plates.

Rib fixation devices: Kirschner wire, Rehbein plate, rib splint [api/images/SFcxL4u0hI5W/rib-fixation-devices.png]

title: Aetiology and Closed (Simple) Pneumothorax
content:
AETIOLOGY AND CLOSED (SIMPLE) PNEUMOTHORAX


AETIOLOGY

 1. Traumatic: blunt or penetrating injuries.
 2. Spontaneous: rupture of a small emphysematous bulla or a tuberculous cavity.
 3. Iatrogenic: positive pressure ventilation with alveolar rupture, or during insertion of a central venous line in the neck.


CLOSED (SIMPLE) PNEUMOTHORAX

 * A small amount of air enters the pleural cavity through a lung laceration, producing variable degrees of lung collapse.
 * Patient complains of chest pain and dyspnea.

Chest examination

 * Decreased respiratory movement on the affected side
 * Unilateral chest bulge
 * Tracheal shift to the opposite side
 * Decreased TVF on the same side
 * Hyper-resonance on percussion
 * Diminished air entry

Investigations

 * Plain X-ray: increased translucency and absence of lung markings on the affected side; the edge of the collapsed lung is usually visible.
 * ABG: may show hypoxia and hypercapnia.

Treatment

 * Small and asymptomatic: conservative until spontaneous absorption of air.
 * Severe dyspnea: intercostal tube connected to an under-water seal through the 2nd intercostal space in the mid-axillary line.

title: Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound)
content:
OPEN PNEUMOTHORAX (SUCKING CHEST WOUND)


AETIOLOGY AND PATHOPHYSIOLOGY

 1. A chest wound allows free communication of air between the pleural space and the atmosphere, so air enters and leaves with respiratory movements.
 2. Severe cardio-respiratory distress with shock, cyanosis and dyspnea results from: paradoxical respiration and mediastinal flutter.
 3. During inspiration the normal lung expands, while on the injured side air is sucked into the pleural cavity (negative intrathoracic pressure) and the lung collapses, interfering with gas exchange (paradoxical respiration), raising CO2 and causing distress.
 4. The mediastinum shifts with each breath (mediastinal flutter).

Open (sucking) pneumothorax pathophysiology [api/images/yBPPQe0Ko2vK/open-pneumothorax-pathophysiology.png]


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * History of chest trauma with marked dyspnea and chest pain.
 * Signs of shock, cyanosis.
 * Chest examination as in simple pneumothorax, plus sucking external chest wound (important) and the sound of air going through the wound.

Chest X-ray: jet-black air on the affected side with absence of broncho-vascular markings (lung collapse); associated fractured ribs may be present. ABG as before.


TREATMENT

 * First aid: close the wound with an adhesive external dressing.
 * Definitive: suture the wound and insert an intercostal tube in the 2nd space, mid-clavicular line.

First aid dressing for a sucking chest wound [api/images/f1XuJuzI4UrT/sucking-chest-wound-first-aid.png]

title: Tension Pneumothorax
content:
TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX

Causes: the same as before.


PATHOPHYSIOLOGY

An opening in the pleural cavity (through the chest wall as a valvular wound, or from the lung) permits entry of air during inspiration but prevents its exit during expiration. Air accumulates under tension:

 1. Compression of the lung with displacement of the heart and mediastinum to the opposite side.
 2. Decreased venous return.
 3. Bilateral lung collapse (total on the affected side, partial on the opposite side) and shock.
 4. Severe cardio-respiratory distress, ending in respiratory failure.

Tension pneumothorax pathophysiology [api/images/5l2YT6KpIv1H/tension-pneumothorax-pathophysiology.png]


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * Symptoms: history of trauma; severe dyspnea and chest pain.
 * General: signs of shock, cyanosis, congested neck veins.
 * Chest: unilateral marked chest expansion; marked decrease in respiratory movement on the affected side; tracheal shift to the opposite side; hyper-resonance; decreased TVF and decreased breath sounds.


INVESTIGATIONS

 * Chest X-ray:
   * Total lung collapse on the affected side with jet-black translucency
   * Partial collapse on the opposite side
   * Tracheal and cardiac shadow shifted to the opposite side
   * Diaphragm depressed on the affected side
   * Fractured ribs may be present
 * ABG: severe hypoxia, hypercapnia and acidosis.


TREATMENT

The condition is rapidly fatal if untreated.

 * Emergency insertion of a wide-bore needle into the pleural cavity in the 2nd intercostal space, replaced later by an intercostal tube in the 2nd space, mid-axillary line.
 * Continuous bubbling of air through the intercostal tube suggests a broncho-pleural fistula, which may need surgical correction.
