title: Acute Empyema
content:
ACUTE EMPYEMA


AETIOLOGY

 * Commonest after lobar pneumonia and lung abscess.
 * Direct access through open wounds.
 * Local spread from chest wall, lung, esophagus.
 * Blood spread, as in septicemia.


ORGANISMS

 1. Staphylococcal empyema: directly from pneumonia or by blood spread from septicemia.
 2. Putrid empyema: follows rupture of the lung or a sub-phrenic abscess; mixed infection (E. coli, Proteus, Pseudomonas).
 3. Pneumococcal empyema.
 4. Streptococcal empyema.


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * Onset usually masked by the original disease (e.g., pneumonia).
 * Marked dyspnea, fever, sweating and toxaemia.
 * Classic signs of fluid in the pleural cavity (as in hemothorax).


INVESTIGATIONS

 * Blood picture: leukocytosis and elevated ESR.
 * Thoracocentesis: reveals pus for culture and sensitivity. Fluid is turbid, pH < 7.2, LDH > 1000, glucose > 40. Gram stain/culture positive for the organism.
 * Chest X-ray: obliterated costophrenic angle with an oblique opacity rising toward the axilla.


TREATMENT

General: antibiotics, good diet, vitamins.

Local (primary options)

 * Recurrent thoracocentesis
 * Chest drain alone or combined with fibrinolytics
 * VATS (video-assisted thoracoscopy): an alternative for multiloculated empyema; the loculations are disrupted with a thoracoscope and the pleural space drained completely. Safe and effective; earlier intervention gives better results.
 * Open decortication: if the pleura remains thickened with symptom-limiting reduction in pulmonary function after about 6 months.

title: Chronic Empyema
content:
CHRONIC EMPYEMA

Definition: empyema in which the lung cannot expand after evacuation of pus because of fibrosis.

CT showing left chronic empyema [api/images/JD52do7qbkGk/chronic-empyema-ct.png]


TREATMENT

General: correct anemia and toxemia with antibiotics and multivitamins.

Local (surgical)

 * VATS debridement: lower postoperative hospital stay, shorter chest drainage, and greater improvement in subjective dyspnea score.
 * Decortication: all the fibrous tissue is removed from the visceral pleural peel and all pus evacuated from the pleural space. Not tolerated by critically ill patients.
 * When the patient is too ill for decortication: rib resection and open drainage. Used when closed-tube drainage is inadequate: 1-3 ribs overlying the lower part of the cavity are resected, a large-bore chest tube is inserted, and drained into a colostomy bag.

title: Principles of Chest Trauma
content:
PRINCIPLES OF CHEST TRAUMA

 * Trauma is the most common cause of death and of short- and long-term disability.
 * 25% of all trauma deaths result from chest injuries alone, while respiratory problems share in 75% of traumatic deaths.


AETIOLOGY AND MECHANISM OF INJURY

 * Blunt trauma: blows to the chest wall, fall from height, motor car accident; ecchymosis or crushing of the chest wall with or without internal injuries.
 * Penetrating trauma: sharp instruments (knives, stabs, gunshots); commonly associated with internal injuries and a sharp external wound.
 * Blast injuries: pressure-wave chest injuries.


PRESENTATION OF CHEST TRAUMA

 1.  Skin injury: cut, contused or crushed wounds
 2.  Chest wall muscles: hematomas
 3.  Fracture ribs (see note)
 4.  Hemothorax (see note)
 5.  Pneumothorax (see note)
 6.  Hemo-pneumothorax
 7.  Lung contusion or laceration
 8.  Cardiac injuries
 9.  Injury to major blood vessels
 10. Diaphragmatic injury
 11. Esophageal injury

title: Hemothorax
content:
HEMOTHORAX

Blood in the pleural space.

Hemothorax [api/images/caGIw8N57Fl2/hemothorax.png]


AETIOLOGY

 1. Traumatic: closed or penetrating chest injuries. Source of bleeding: intercostal vessels, internal mammary vessels, sometimes the lung.
 2. Postoperative: after cardiac, pulmonary or esophageal operations.
 3. Pathological: tumors of the lung, pleura or mediastinum; leaking aortic aneurysm.


PATHOLOGY

 * Blood in the pleural space is an irritant and excites formation of a protein-rich effusion, increasing the fluid volume.
 * Respiratory and cardiac movements defibrinate the blood, so it stays fluid (delayed clotting).
 * In neglected cases, fibrin is deposited on both pleural layers and turns into fibrous tissue, causing lung collapse and chest deformity, with rib crowding.
 * Blood is a good medium for organisms: infected hemothorax.


CLINICAL PICTURE

 * Symptoms: history of chest trauma or thoracic surgery; chest pain and dyspnea.
 * General: rapid pulse, subnormal temperature, hypotension; sweating and coldness (hypovolemic shock); increasing pallor and cyanosis.
 * Inspection: unilateral chest bulge on the affected side; decreased expansion; ecchymosis at the trauma site.
 * Palpation: trachea deviated to the opposite side (mediastinal shift); decreased TVF.
 * Percussion: dullness on the affected side.
 * Auscultation: decreased air entry.


INVESTIGATIONS: PLAIN CHEST X-RAY

 1. Obliteration of the costophrenic angle (< 500 cc)
 2. Opacity rising to the axilla (> 500 cc)
 3. Mediastinal shift to the opposite side
 4. May show hemo-pneumothorax (air and fluid level)
 5. May show associated fractured ribs
 6. In complicated cases with fibrothorax: crowding of the ribs and narrowed spaces

Hemo-pneumothorax on chest X-ray [api/images/cyB0OKzg0DDq/hemo-pneumothorax-xray.png]


TREATMENT

 1. Aim: drain blood from the pleural space to allow lung expansion.
 2. Correct hypovolemic shock (IV fluids, sedation, blood transfusion).
 3. Analgesics for pain.
 4. Chest tube
    * Usually inserted in the 5th intercostal space in the mid-axillary line, connected to an under-water seal.
    * Allows drainage and monitoring of the amount of bleeding.
    * Conservative management continues as long as the patient is vitally stable (normal pulse and BP), the amount of blood is decreasing, and the lung is expanding.
    * Remove the tube when no more blood is coming and the lung is fully expanded.

Chest tube insertion [api/images/Q8p4rfgyTUt3/chest-tube-insertion.png]


INDICATIONS FOR THORACOTOMY IN HEMOTHORAX

 1. Massive bleeding (> 200 cc/hour)
 2. Clotted hemothorax: the tube fails to drain blood with continuous lung collapse
 3. Associated injuries, e.g., esophagus
 4. Foreign bodies in the chest

title: Arterial blood gases (ABG)
content:
ARTERIAL BLOOD GASES (ABG)

غازات الدم الشرياني

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

تحليل عينة دم شرياني لقياس الأكسجين وثاني أكسيد الكربون وpH (PaO2, PaCO2, pH).


ما هو وكيف يُجرى (WHAT & HOW)

عينة شريانية بمضاد تخثر وتُحلل فورا أو توضع في ماء مثلج.


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * PaO2 أقل من 8 kPa = نقص أكسجة. PaCO2 أكثر من 7 kPa = فشل تنفسي نوع II.
 * نوبة الربو: ارتفاع CO2 أو CO2 طبيعي مع إنهاك = علامة خطر.
 * pH منخفض مع CO2 مرتفع = حموضة تنفسية.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.6 Acute Severe Asthma (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Measure arterial blood gases if any of these are present or if oxygen saturation is < 92%.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Blood gases: often normal at rest. In advanced cases hypoxemia, possibly hypercapnia.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Hypoxemia: PaO2 < 8 kPa and need for assisted ventilation
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): ABG for severity.

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.1 Definition, Causes and Types: In practical terms: PaO2 < 8 kPa (60 mmHg) or PaCO2 > 7 kPa (55 mmHg).
 * 6.2 Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment: Arterial blood gas (ABG): guides oxygen therapy and objectively assesses severity. The sample must be adequately anticoagulated …
 * 6.3 ARDS: ABG: respiratory acidosis and hypoxemia that does not respond to increased % of O2.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.2 Flail Chest (7.2 Fracture Ribs): ABG: decreased PO2 and increased PCO2; pH decreased in severe cases; respiratory failure may be evident.
 * 7.4.1 Aetiology and Closed (Simple) Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): ABG: may show hypoxia and hypercapnia.
 * 7.4.2 Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound) (7.4 Pneumothorax): Chest X-ray: jet-black air on the affected side with absence of broncho-vascular markings (lung collapse); associated fractured ribs may be present. ABG as before.
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): ABG: severe hypoxia, hypercapnia and acidosis.

title: Bacterial identification tests (Optochin, Bile solubility, Oxidase, Catalase, Indole)
content:
BACTERIAL IDENTIFICATION TESTS (OPTOCHIN, BILE SOLUBILITY, OXIDASE, CATALASE, INDOLE)

اختبارات تحديد الجراثيم

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

اختبارات بسيطة تفرق جرثومة عن أخرى (simple discriminating tests).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * Optochin وbile solubility وinulin: المكورات الرئوية مقابل العقديات الخضراء.
 * Oxidase موجب: Pseudomonas، سالب: Acinetobacter.
 * Catalase سالب للمكورات الرئوية.
 * Indole سالب (IMVC --++): Klebsiella.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.3 Typical Bacterial Pathogens (Pneumococcus and Haemophilus) (3.1 Pneumonia): Culture: enriched media, 5-10% CO2 (capnophilic), 37°C; produces alpha-hemolytic colonies. Very fragile; contains the enzyme autolysin, so it dissolves in bile.
 * 3.1.8 Nosocomial Pathogens (Klebsiella, Serratia, Pseudomonas) (3.1 Pneumonia): Biochemical: ferments all sugars with acid and gas; indole negative.

Microbe Files (بطاقات الميكروبات)

 * Streptococcus pneumoniae: البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions) Catalase سالب، يخمّر inulin، يعطي انحلال دم ألفا (alpha-hemolysis) على آجار الدم (blood agar)، حساس للأوبتوكين، يذوب في الصفراء (bile)
 * Klebsiella pneumoniae: البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions) تخمّر الجلوكوز واللاكتوز والمالتوز والمانيتول والسكروز والساليسين بإنتاج حمض وغاز. Indole سالب، methyl red سالب، VP موجب، citrate موجب (IMVC: --++)
 * Pseudomonas aeruginosa: البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions) لا تخمّر الكربوهيدرات، تنتج حمضا من الجلوكوز بالأكسدة (بلا غاز)، Oxidase موجب، Indole سالب
 * Acinetobacter baumannii: البصمة الكيميائية (Biochemical reactions) Oxidase سالب، غير مخمّرة

title: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)
content:
BRONCHOALVEOLAR LAVAGE (BAL)

الغسيل القصبي السنخي

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

يُضخ ماء مالح عبر المنظار في جزء من الرئة ثم يُسحب لفحص الخلايا والجراثيم (lavage fluid analysis).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

في ILD تتغير أعداد الخلايا غالبا بلا تشخيص نوعي، وفي العدوى يكشف الجراثيم.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.4.2 Diagnosis and Investigations (1.4 Lung Abscess): Microbiological culture, ideally before starting antibiotics. Also useful to exclude tuberculosis. Blood cultures; sputum or bronchoscopy specimen (BAL needed).

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

title: Bronchoscopy

منظار القصبات

title: Chest X-ray (CXR)
content:
CHEST X-RAY (CXR)

أشعة الصدر البسيطة

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

أول فحص تصويري يُجرى لأغلب أمراض الصدر (the first imaging test).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * الربو: غالبا طبيعية، وفرط انتفاخ في النوبة.
 * COPD: فرط انتفاخ، حجاب منخفض ومسطح، وقد تظهر فقاعات (bullae).
 * ILD: ظل زجاجي ثم شبكي عقيدي (reticulonodular).
 * الالتهاب الرئوي: تصلب (consolidation) وأحيانا انصباب.
 * السل: ارتشاح في الفص العلوي مع تجاويف.
 * الانصباب: انطماس الزاوية الضلعية الحجابية (يظهر عند 300 mL تقريبا).
 * استرواح الصدر: شفافية سوداء بلا علامات أوعية.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.4 Clinical Presentation and Investigations (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Chest X-ray: no diagnostic features of asthma, although overinflation is characteristic during an acute episode.
 * 1.1.6 Acute Severe Asthma (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Chest X-ray to rule out pneumothorax.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Chest X-ray: often normal. In advanced cases: overinflation with low flattened diaphragms, sometimes large bullae.
 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Chest X-ray: may be normal, or show dilated bronchi with thickened walls and sometimes multiple fluid-containing cysts.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): HRCT chest, fiberoptic bronchoscopy for endobronchial lesions, sputum culture, CXR for follow-up.
 * 1.4.2 Diagnosis and Investigations (1.4 Lung Abscess): The diagnosis is usually made from the history together with a cavity with an air-fluid level on chest X-ray.

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.1.1 Definition and Classification (2.1 ILD Overview): … between blood and air. Normally it is so thin it cannot be seen on a chest X-ray.
 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): Chest X-ray: usually the first test, but can be normal early. Initially a diffuse ground-glass pattern, then reticulonodular shadowing.
 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Löfgren syndrome: bilateral hilar adenopathy on chest radiograph + erythema nodosum + periarticular inflammation or arthritis of the ankles.
 * 2.4.4 Staging and Investigations (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Imaging: chest X-ray and HRCT assess diffuse parenchymal involvement and detect small nodules.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Radiology: bilateral or multilobe involvement; progression of CXR changes in ICU
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): Fever; productive cough; raised inflammatory parameters; new CXR infiltrate; deterioration in gas exchange. Diagnosis is often clinical; identifying the organism can be hard,…
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): CXR (usually first): upper lobe infiltrates with cavitation, possibly hilar or paratracheal lymphadenopathy; old TB shows fibrous scarring and calcification.

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.4 Investigations and Treatment (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Radiology: chest X-ray and CT.

Chapter 5: Pleural effusion

 * 5.1 Clinical Picture and Radiology: Detected on X-ray when 300 mL or more of fluid is present, and clinically when 500 mL or more.

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.2 Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment: Chest X-ray: pneumonia, pneumothorax, pulmonary embolism, ILD.
 * 6.3 ARDS: …creased vascular permeability; bilateral and extensive infiltrates on CXR; very poor oxygenation; not due to clinical left ventricular failure. It results in acute respiratory failure…

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.1 Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures (7.2 Fracture Ribs): Investigations: plain chest X-ray (number and sites of fractures; detects hemo- or pneumothorax); abdominal ultrasound and CT for suspected injuries elsewhere.
 * 7.2.2 Flail Chest (7.2 Fracture Ribs): Plain X-ray: multiple fractured ribs at 2 sites on the same side; may show hemo- or pneumothorax.
 * 7.4.1 Aetiology and Closed (Simple) Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Plain X-ray: increased translucency and absence of lung markings on the affected side; the edge of the collapsed lung is usually visible.
 * 7.4.2 Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound) (7.4 Pneumothorax): Chest X-ray: jet-black air on the affected side with absence of broncho-vascular markings (lung collapse); associated fractured ribs may be present. ABG as before.
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Chest X-ray:
 * 7.5.1 Acute Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): Chest X-ray: obliterated costophrenic angle with an oblique opacity rising toward the axilla.

title: CT and High-resolution CT (HRCT)
content:
CT AND HIGH-RESOLUTION CT (HRCT)

الأشعة المقطعية عالية الدقة

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

تصوير مقطعي بشرائح رقيقة جدا (1-1.5 mm) تعطي دقة أعلى بنحو 10 أضعاف (thin-slice CT).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * توسع القصبات: توسع القصبات وفقدان تدرجها، حساسية تتجاوز 90-97%.
 * ILD: أفضل وسيلة لتصنيف الأنماط.
 * COPD: يُظهر فقاعات الانتفاخ.
 * الورم والخراج والدبيلة: يحدد الموضع والامتداد ويوجه الخزعة.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): High-resolution CT: particularly to show emphysematous bullae.
 * 1.3.1 Definition and Etiology (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Clinically: cough with production of large amounts of sputum, and dilated, thickened bronchi seen on CT. It is one of the suppurative lung diseases.
 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): High-resolution CT: bronchial dilatation with loss of airway tapering at the periphery, wall thickening, cysts at the ends of bronchioles; sensitivity 97%.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): HRCT chest, fiberoptic bronchoscopy for endobronchial lesions, sputum culture, CXR for follow-up.
 * 1.4.2 Diagnosis and Investigations (1.4 Lung Abscess): CT if the diagnosis is in doubt; it also defines the exact position of the abscess (useful for physiotherapy, or if surgery is considered, which is rarely needed).

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): High-resolution CT (HRCT): the preferred modality. Conventional CT examines 7-10 mm slices at 10 mm intervals; HRCT examines 1-1.5 mm …
 * 2.2 Hypersensitivity Pneumonitis: Based on history of antigen exposure plus typical clinical and HRCT features.
 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): …aise and arthralgia; benign course. Exclude TB and lymphoma (may need HRCT and lymph node aspirate or biopsy).
 * 2.4.4 Staging and Investigations (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Imaging: chest X-ray and HRCT assess diffuse parenchymal involvement and detect small nodules.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): CT chest: unlikely to add information; useful if diagnosis in doubt or the patient is severely ill and failing to resp…
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): CT is more sensitive than CXR, especially for small areas.

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.4 Investigations and Treatment (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Radiology: chest X-ray and CT.

Chapter 5: Pleural effusion

 * 5.3 Chylothorax and Empyema: …choscopy, or percutaneous transthoracic aspiration with ultrasound or CT guidance.

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.3 ARDS: …re hypoxemia, stiff lungs, and widespread diffuse infiltrates on CXR; CT shows diffuse alveolar infiltrates and air bronchograms.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.1 Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures (7.2 Fracture Ribs): Investigations: plain chest X-ray (number and sites of fractures; detects hemo- or pneumothorax); abdominal ultrasound and CT for suspected injuries elsewhere.

title: CURB-65 severity score
content:
CURB-65 SEVERITY SCORE

درجة CURB-65

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

title: Gas transfer - DLCO
content:
GAS TRANSFER / DLCO

قدرة نقل الغاز

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

قياس قدرة الرئة على نقل الغاز من الحويصلات إلى الدم باستنشاق CO بتركيز قليل (carbon monoxide transfer).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

تنخفض في ILD وانتفاخ الرئة والأمراض الوعائية الرئوية، وتكون طبيعية نسبيا في الربو.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): Pulmonary function tests usually show a restrictive defect with decreased diffusion capacity (DLCO).
 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): …Lung function may be normal or show a restrictive defect with reduced transfer factor.
 * 2.4.4 Staging and Investigations (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Lung function: restrictive defect in pulmonary infiltration: decreased TLC, decreased FEV1 and FVC, decreased gas transfer. Usually normal in extrapulmonary disease or hilar adenopathy only.

title: Gram stain
content:
GRAM STAIN

صبغة جرام

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

صبغة تفرق الجراثيم موجبة الجرام (بنفسجية) عن سالبتها (وردية) (differential bacterial stain).


ما هو وكيف يُجرى (WHAT & HOW)

تُصبغ مسحة من البلغم وتُفحص تحت المجهر.


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

تشخيصية للمكورات الرئوية (مكورات موجبة ثنائية). لا تصبغ Mycoplasma وChlamydia (تُصبغ بـ Giemsa) ولا عصية السل (تُصبغ بـ ZN).


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.3 Typical Bacterial Pathogens (Pneumococcus and Haemophilus) (3.1 Pneumonia): Gram-stained smear is diagnostic; capsular polysaccharide antigen by latex agglutination.
 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): …tic choice and limits resistance. In outpatients, pretreatment sputum Gram stain, culture and blood cultures are not recommended. They are crucial in hospital patients, especially severe CAP…

title: Inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP, WBC)
content:
INFLAMMATORY MARKERS (ESR, CRP, WBC)

مؤشرات الالتهاب

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

تحاليل دم ترتفع مع الالتهاب والعدوى (blood tests of inflammation).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * WBC أكثر من 15×1000 = عدوى بكتيرية (مكورية رئوية).
 * WBC أكثر من 20 أو أقل من 4 = عدوى شديدة.
 * CRP أدق من الحرارة وWBC ويتابع الاستجابة.
 * ESR مرتفع في الساركويد والسل.

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.4.4 Staging and Investigations (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Full blood count: mild normochromic normocytic anemia with raised ESR or CRP.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.1 Definition, Classification and Routes of Infection (3.1 Pneumonia): The IDSA defines pneumonia as a new lung infiltrate with other clinical evidence supporting infection: new fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis, and decline in oxygenation.
 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): White cell count > 20 or < 4 ×1000/L
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): A new radiographic infiltrate with evidence of infection (fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis) with onset at least 48 hours after hospital admission.

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.4 Investigations and Treatment (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Other: full blood count (anemia) and biochemistry (liver involvement, hypercalcemia, hyponatremia).

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.2 Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment: Complete blood count: leukocytosis.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.5.1 Acute Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): Blood picture: leukocytosis and elevated ESR.

title: Peak expiratory flow rate (PEFR)
content:
PEAK EXPIRATORY FLOW RATE (PEFR)

أقصى سرعة زفير

أقصى سرعة هواء في الزفير القسري، يقاس بجهاز صغير محمول (peak flow meter).

ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

تقلب القراءة بين الصباح والمساء وعبر الأيام يدل على الربو (variable airflow limitation). يساعد المريض على متابعة مرضه ذاتيا.

title: Serology (Complement fixation, ELISA, haemagglutination inhibition)
content:
SEROLOGY (COMPLEMENT FIXATION, ELISA, HAEMAGGLUTINATION INHIBITION)

الفحوص المصلية

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

قياس الأجسام المضادة في الدم لإثبات عدوى حديثة (measuring antibodies).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * ارتفاع العيار أربعة أضعاف في عينتين متباعدتين = عدوى حديثة.
 * IgM مرتفع = عدوى حديثة.
 * Complement fixation: لا يبلغ الذروة قبل 4-6 أسابيع (Mycoplasma).
 * Haemagglutination inhibition: الإنفلونزا.

 * 3.1.4 Atypical Pathogens (Mycoplasma, Legionella, Chlamydia) (3.1 Pneumonia): Serology: complement fixation (titer peaks 4-6 weeks; fourfold rise = recent infection); ELISA for IgM.
 * 3.1.5 Viral Pneumonias (Influenza, Coronaviruses, COVID-19) (3.1 Pneumonia): Diagnosis (respiratory secretions): immunofluorescence; viral isolation in cell culture or eggs; serology by haemagglutination inhibition.
 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Viral and atypical pathogens only in severe CAP: serology on paired samples, and in those unresponsive to β-lactams.
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): Serology is of little use.
 * 3.2.3 Laboratory Diagnosis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): b. QuantiFERON-Gold TB / interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs): measure IFN-gamma released by sensitized T lymphocytes in whole blood when exposed to TB antigens, detected by ELISA.

title: Special culture media (Chocolate agar, BCYE, L-J, MacConkey, Blood agar)
content:
SPECIAL CULTURE MEDIA (CHOCOLATE AGAR, BCYE, L-J, MACCONKEY, BLOOD AGAR)

أوساط الزرع الخاصة

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

كل جرثومة تحتاج وسطا خاصا (each organism needs a specific medium).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * Chocolate agar: المستدمية النزلية (عاملا X وV).
 * BCYE: Legionella (تحتاج السيستين ولا تنمو على آجار الدم).
 * Lowenstein-Jensen: عصية السل (بيض وmalachite green).
 * MacConkey: يفرق مخمرات اللاكتوز (Klebsiella) عن غير المخمرة (Pseudomonas).
 * Blood agar: انحلال الدم (S. pneumoniae ألفا).
 * Serum-enriched agar: Mycoplasma («البيضة المقلية»).


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

title: Spirometry (FEV1, FVC, FEV1 -FVC)
content:
SPIROMETRY (FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC)

قياس التنفس

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

جهاز ينفخ فيه المريض بأقصى قوة ليقيس حجم الهواء وسرعته (measures lung volumes and airflow).


ما هو وكيف يُجرى (WHAT & HOW)

FVC: كل الهواء الذي يُزفر بقوة. FEV1: ما يخرج في الثانية الأولى. النسبة FEV1/FVC تفرّق الانسداد عن التقييد.


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * انسدادي (obstructive): FEV1/FVC أقل من 0.70 بعد موسع الشعب = COPD؛ وفي الربو يتحسن FEV1 أكثر من 15% بعد الموسع.
 * تقييدي (restrictive): الحجوم كلها منخفضة والنسبة طبيعية أو مرتفعة = ILD.
 * مراحل GOLD في COPD حسب FEV1 (% من المتوقع).


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.4 Clinical Presentation and Investigations (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Spirometry: useful especially for assessing reversibility. Asthma is diagnosed by a >15% improvement in FEV1 after inhaling a bronchodilator.
 * 1.1.5 Management of Chronic Asthma (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Restore normal or best possible lung function.
 * 1.1.7 Asthma in Brief and Viva Questions (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): …ment with inhaled steroids gives long-lasting control of mild asthma (FEV1 more than 85% of predicted). Maintenance can usually be given at a reduced dose; discontinuation is often pos…
 * 1.2.1 Definition and Risk Factors (1.2 COPD): Infections: severe childhood respiratory infection is associated with reduced lung function and more respiratory symptoms in adulthood.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Spirometry is required to make the diagnosis: a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70 confirms persistent airflow limitation.
 * 1.2.7 Management of COPD (1.2 COPD): Bronchodilators (increase FEV1 and/or change other spirometry variables)
 * 1.3.4 Treatment and Complications (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Antibiotics: if sputum remains yellow or green despite regular physiotherapy, or if lung function deteriorates despite bronchodilators.

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): Pulmonary function tests usually show a restrictive defect with decreased diffusion capacity (DLCO).
 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): …can return to normal or progress to fibrosis and respiratory failure. Lung function may be normal or show a restrictive defect with reduced transfer factor.
 * 2.4.4 Staging and Investigations (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Lung function: restrictive defect in pulmonary infiltration: decreased TLC, decreased FEV1 and FVC, decreased gas transfer. Usually normal in extrapulmonary disease or hilar adenopathy only.
 * 2.4.5 Treatment (2.4 Sarcoidosis): The decision to treat is usually based on symptoms and, when the lungs are involved, a decline in pulmonary function.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.5.1 Acute Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): Open decortication: if the pleura remains thickened with symptom-limiting reduction in pulmonary function after about 6 months.

title: Tuberculin skin test (Mantoux)
content:
TUBERCULIN SKIN TEST (MANTOUX)

اختبار السلين

النوع (Type): أداة تشخيص (Diagnostic tool)


التعريف | DEFINITION

حقن 0.1 mL من PPD (5 وحدات) داخل الجلد في الساعد وقياس التصلب بعد 48-72 ساعة (induration, not erythema).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

 * إيجابي عند ≥ 5 mm: مصابون سابقون، مخالطون، مرضى HIV.
 * ≥ 10 mm: مناطق موبوءة، السكري، أطفال غير مطعمين أقل من 4 سنوات.
 * ≥ 15 mm: بلا عوامل خطر.
 * سلبي كاذب: عدوى مبكرة، anergy، كبت المناعة.
 * إيجابي كاذب: جراثيم غير سلية (NTM)، تطعيم BCG.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

 * 3.2.2 Pathogenesis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Frequency ~90% of those with positive tuberculin test ~10%
 * 3.2.3 Laboratory Diagnosis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): a. Tuberculin test (Mantoux)
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Tuberculin skin test: useful only if strongly positive (suggesting active disease) or negative; interpret with clinical picture, ethnic origin, exposure and BCG history.

Α1-ANTITRYPSIN LEVEL AND GENOTYPE

مستوى ألفا-1 أنتيتربسين

قياس مستوى البروتين الكبدي الذي يحمي الرئة من الإنزيمات الهادمة (alpha-1 antitrypsin level).


ماذا يكشف وكيف يُفسَّر (WHAT IT SHOWS)

يُطلب في COPD المبكر أو عند غير المدخنين أو في تاريخ عائلي. مستوى أقل من 20% يوحي بنقص متماثل الزيجوت (homozygous).

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.2.1 Definition and Risk Factors (1.2 COPD): Genetic factors: severe hereditary deficiency of alpha-1 antitrypsin (AATD). Family members should be screened; a level < 20% of normal strongly suggests homozygous deficiency.
 * 1.2.4 Emphysema (Pathology) (1.2 COPD): Panacinar (panlobular) All portions of the acinus (not of the entire lung) Most often with α1-antitrypsin deficiency in middle-aged smokers
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): α1-antitrypsin levels and genotype: especially in premature disease or non-smokers.
 * 1.2.7 Management of COPD (1.2 COPD): α1-antitrypsin replacement: weekly or monthly infusions for patients with serum levels below 310 mg/L and abnormal lung function.

title: Anti-IgE and Anti-IL5 (biologic therapy)

ANTI-IGE AND ANTI-IL5 (BIOLOGIC THERAPY)

الأدوية البيولوجية ضد IgE وIL-5

التعريف | DEFINITION

أجسام مضادة أحادية النسيلة تُعطى بالحقن للربو الشديد (monoclonal antibodies for severe asthma).


الفئة والمفعول (CLASS & ACTION)

anti-IgE يربط IgE الحر فيمنع تحسس الخلايا البدينة (atopic asthma). anti-IL5 يقلل الحمضات (eosinophilic asthma). والعلاج المناعي (immunotherapy) يعوّد الجسم تدريجيا على المسبب.


الاستعمال في المنهج (USE IN THIS COURSE)

الدرجة 5 في الربو، مع جرعة منخفضة من الكورتيزون الفموي أحيانا.

title: Isoniazid (INH)
content:
ISONIAZID (INH)

أيزونيازيد

النوع (Type): دواء (Drug)


التعريف | DEFINITION

الفئة والمفعول (CLASS & ACTION)

يثبط تصنيع mycolic acid في جدار عصية السل، ويعمل داخل الخلايا وخارجها. يُكسر في الكبد بـ acetylation (سريع أو بطيء).


الاستعمال في المنهج (USE IN THIS COURSE)

title: Penicillins (Penicillin, Benzylpenicillin, Amoxicillin, Ampicillin)
content:
PENICILLINS (PENICILLIN, BENZYLPENICILLIN, AMOXICILLIN, AMPICILLIN)

البنسلينات

النوع (Type): دواء (Drug)


التعريف | DEFINITION

مضادات حيوية β-lactam قاتلة للجراثيم (bactericidal β-lactams).


الفئة والمفعول (CLASS & ACTION)

تمنع بناء جدار الخلية البكتيرية (cell-wall synthesis) فتنفجر الجرثومة.


الاستعمال في المنهج (USE IN THIS COURSE)

البنسلين هو الدواء المفضل للمكورات الرئوية. أموكسيسيلين في الالتهاب الرئوي المكتسب من المجتمع. لا تنفع ضد Mycoplasma وChlamydia (لا جدار/لا peptidoglycan). Klebsiella مقاومة للأمبيسلين طبيعيا.


أعراض جانبية وتنبيهات (SIDE EFFECTS & CAUTIONS)

الحساسية (rash، وحتى صدمة تحسسية). عند حساسية البنسلين تُستعمل السيفالوسبورينات أو الماكروليدات.

title: SABA - Short-acting β2-agonists (Salbutamol, Terbutaline, Fenoterol)
content:
SABA: SHORT-ACTING Β2-AGONISTS (SALBUTAMOL, TERBUTALINE, FENOTEROL)

منبهات بيتا-2 قصيرة المفعول

النوع (Type): دواء (Drug)


التعريف | DEFINITION

موسّعات شعب إسعافية تعمل خلال دقائق وتستمر نحو 4-6 ساعات (rapid-onset bronchodilators, 'relievers').


الفئة والمفعول (CLASS & ACTION)

تنبه مستقبلات β2 في عضلات القصبات فيرتفع cyclic AMP فتسترخي العضلة ويتسع المجرى. تحسن أيضا تنظيف المخاط (mucociliary clearance). لا تعالج الالتهاب المزمن.


الاستعمال في المنهج (USE IN THIS COURSE)

إسعاف الربو وCOPD عند الأعراض، وبالرذاذ (nebulizer) في نوبة الربو الشديدة. زيادة الحاجة إليها = تدهور المرض.


أعراض جانبية وتنبيهات (SIDE EFFECTS & CAUTIONS)

title: Systemic corticosteroids (Prednisolone, Hydrocortisone)
content:
SYSTEMIC CORTICOSTEROIDS (PREDNISOLONE, HYDROCORTISONE)

الكورتيزون الجهازي

النوع (Type): دواء (Drug)


التعريف | DEFINITION

أدوية مضادة للالتهاب والمناعة تؤخذ بالفم أو الوريد (potent anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive).


الفئة والمفعول (CLASS & ACTION)

تقلل نفاذية الأوعية وتجمع العدلات والحمضات وتثبط الخلايا الليفية والاستجابة المناعية.


الاستعمال في المنهج (USE IN THIS COURSE)

نوبة الربو الحادة، تفاقم COPD، التهاب الرئة التحسسي (prednisolone 40-60 mg يوميا لشهر ثم تخفيض)، الساركويد (30 mg ست أسابيع)، ILD.


أعراض جانبية وتنبيهات (SIDE EFFECTS & CAUTIONS)

التهاب المعدة وقرحتها، السكري، ارتفاع الضغط، العدوى الفطرية، كبت المناعة، تثبيط الغدة الكظرية، ملامح كوشينغ (Cushingoid)، هشاشة العظام.

 * 1.2.7 Management of COPD (1.2 COPD): Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) combined with a long-acting bronchodilator: in moderate to very severe COPD with exacerbations, ICS + L…
 * 1.3.4 Treatment and Complications (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Anti-inflammatory agents: inhaled or oral steroids can slow progression.

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.4.5 Treatment (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Prednisolone 30 mg for 6 weeks, then reduced to alternate-day prednisolone 15 mg for 6-12 months, according to response.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Oral steroids / immunosuppression: Legionella may be more common.
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Medical factors: diabetes, renal disease, malignancy, systemic chemotherapy, corticosteroids, new immunosuppressant drugs

title: Cough
content:
COUGH

السعال

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

انعكاس يطرد الهواء والمفرزات بقوة من الجهاز التنفسي (a protective reflex to clear the airway).


أنواعه (TYPES)

 * جاف (dry / non-productive): ILD، Mycoplasma، الفيروسات، الربو أحيانا.
 * منتج للبلغم (productive): COPD، توسع القصبات، الالتهاب الرئوي، خراج الرئة.
 * ليلي أو صباحي: الربو.
 * مستمر أكثر من أسبوعين: يُشتبه بالسل (TB).
 * سعال «البقر» (bovine cough): شلل العصب الحنجري الراجع بسبب ورم.


اسأل عن (ASK ABOUT)

المدة، الوقت، لون البلغم وكميته، وجود دم، علاقته بالمجهود أو الحساسية أو التدخين.

 * 1.3.2 Pathology (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Once developed, it gives a symptom complex dominated by cough and expectoration of conspicuous amounts of purulent sputum.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Cough with copious purulent sputum, recurrent hemoptysis.

 * Aspergillus: …لا تسبب أعراض (symptoms)ا. وعدوى الرشاشيات الغازية السريعة تسبب سعال (cough)ا وحمى (fever) وألم صدر وصعوبة تنفس

title: Cyanosis
content:
CYANOSIS

الزرقة

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

لون أزرق في الشفتين واللسان والأظافر بسبب زيادة الهيموغلوبين غير المؤكسج (bluish discolouration).


المعنى (MEANING)

علامة متأخرة لنقص الأكسجين (hypoxemia) وتظهر عندما يكون الهيموغلوبين المختزل أكثر من 5 g/dL تقريبا.


أين تُرى (SEEN IN)

فشل تنفسي، ILD المتقدم، نوبة الربو المهددة للحياة، أمراض القلب الخلقية الزرقاء.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.6 Acute Severe Asthma (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Silent chest, cyanosis or feeble respiratory effort.

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): Progressive breathlessness, non-productive cough and cyanosis, which eventually lead to respiratory failure, pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.2 Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment: Cyanosis: bluish coloration of mucous membranes and nail beds

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.2 Flail Chest (7.2 Fracture Ribs): General: signs of shock; pallor, cyanosis; associated injuries.
 * 7.3 Hemothorax: General: rapid pulse, subnormal temperature, hypotension; sweating and coldness (hypovolemic shock); increasing pallor and cyanosis.
 * 7.4.2 Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound) (7.4 Pneumothorax): Severe cardio-respiratory distress with shock, cyanosis and dyspnea results from: paradoxical respiration and mediastinal flutter.
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): General: signs of shock, cyanosis, congested neck veins.

title: Dyspnea (Breathlessness)
content:
DYSPNEA (BREATHLESSNESS)

ضيق النفس

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

إحساس المريض بصعوبة أو عدم راحة في التنفس (a subjective feeling of difficult breathing).


لماذا يحدث (MECHANISM)

يزيد جهد التنفس أو تنبه الأعصاب الحسية عند: انسداد المجاري الهوائية (obstruction)، تيبس الرئة (restriction)، نقص الأكسجين، زيادة CO2، أو أسباب قلبية وجنبية.


كيف تسأل عنه (HOW TO ASK)

هل يحدث مع المجهود أم في الراحة؟ تدريجي أم مفاجئ؟ هل يوقظ من النوم؟ في COPD الشديد يحدث حتى عند ارتداء الملابس.


الدلالة (PATTERN)

 * تضيّق انسدادي (obstructive): الربو، COPD — مع صفير (wheeze).
 * تقييدي (restrictive): الأمراض الخلالية ILD — مع سعال جاف وخراخر.
 * جنبي: انصباب الجنب، استرواح الصدر.
 * مفاجئ وشديد: استرواح توتري، جلطة، نوبة ربو شديدة.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.1 Definition and Classification (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): …f the bronchi, causing symptoms of cough, wheeze, chest tightness and dyspnea.
 * 1.1.7 Asthma in Brief and Viva Questions (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Is there reversible airway obstruction? Are the wheezing and breathlessness reversible?
 * 1.2.2 Pathophysiology (1.2 COPD): Summary: each mechanism narrows the small airways and causes air trapping, leading to hyperinflation of the lungs and breathlessness.
 * 1.2.5 Clinical Features (1.2 COPD): Most common symptoms: dyspnea, cough, sputum production, wheezing. Dyspnea on exertion progresses gradually over time.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Consider COPD in any patient with progressive dyspnea, chronic cough or sputum production, with a history of exposure to risk factors.
 * 1.2.7 Management of COPD (1.2 COPD): Pulmonary rehabilitation: modest increase in exercise capacity, less breathlessness, better well-being.
 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Breathlessness from airflow limitation.
 * 1.4.1 Definition, Pathophysiology and Presentation (1.4 Lung Abscess): Breathlessness

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.1.2 Clinical Features and Investigations (2.1 ILD Overview): Onset at age 50 or older (IPF), dry cough, dyspnea, end-inspiratory rales.
 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Interstitial lung involvement: may be asymptomatic or cause dyspnea, cough, chest ache or pain, malaise, fatigue. Rarely crackles or clubbing. Infiltrates on CXR can return to n…

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Fever, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain.
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Breathlessness

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.3 Clinical Features (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Dyspnea and shortness of breath.

Chapter 5: Pleural effusion

 * 5.1 Clinical Picture and Radiology: The usual symptom of a large effusion is shortness of breath, often with a dull ache on the affected side.

Chapter 6: Respiratory failure

 * 6.2 Monitoring, Investigations and Treatment: …reathing. Improves respiratory acidosis, reduces respiratory rate and dyspnea, reduces complications and hospital stay, decreases mortality and need for intubation.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.1 Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures (7.2 Fracture Ribs): In multiple fractures, severe pain with limited respiratory expansion causes dyspnea; dyspnea may be severe if complicated by hemothorax or pneumothorax.
 * 7.2.2 Flail Chest (7.2 Fracture Ribs): Symptoms: history of severe chest trauma; marked chest pain; shortness of breath.
 * 7.3 Hemothorax: Symptoms: history of chest trauma or thoracic surgery; chest pain and dyspnea.
 * 7.4.1 Aetiology and Closed (Simple) Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Patient complains of chest pain and dyspnea.
 * 7.4.2 Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound) (7.4 Pneumothorax): Severe cardio-respiratory distress with shock, cyanosis and dyspnea results from: paradoxical respiration and mediastinal flutter.
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Symptoms: history of trauma; severe dyspnea and chest pain.
 * 7.5.1 Acute Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): Marked dyspnea, fever, sweating and toxaemia.
 * 7.5.2 Chronic Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): VATS debridement: lower postoperative hospital stay, shorter chest drainage, and greater improvement in subjective dyspnea score.

title: Fever (Pyrexia)
content:
FEVER (PYREXIA)

الحمى

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

ارتفاع حرارة الجسم استجابة لعدوى أو التهاب (raised body temperature).


الدلالة (SIGNIFICANCE)

 * عدوى بكتيرية أو فيروسية (الالتهاب الرئوي، الإنفلونزا).
 * السل: حمى خفيفة مع تعرق ليلي (low-grade fever).
 * خراج أو دبيلة: حمى عالية مع تسمم (toxaemia).
 * قد تغيب عند كبار السن.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.7 Asthma in Brief and Viva Questions (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Exacerbations with fever and yellowish sputum.
 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Persistent halitosis, recurrent febrile episodes with malaise, episodes of pneumonia.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Intermittent fever and night sweats.
 * 1.4.1 Definition, Pathophysiology and Presentation (1.4 Lung Abscess): Fevers, night sweats

Chapter 2: Interstitial lung diseases

 * 2.4.3 Clinical Features (2.4 Sarcoidosis): Fever, fatigue, weight loss; peripheral lymphadenopathy with hepatic enlargement and splenomegaly.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.1 Definition, Classification and Routes of Infection (3.1 Pneumonia): The IDSA defines pneumonia as a new lung infiltrate with other clinical evidence supporting infection: new fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis, and decline in oxygenation.
 * 3.1.4 Atypical Pathogens (Mycoplasma, Legionella, Chlamydia) (3.1 Pneumonia): Symptoms: fever, headache, non-productive cough.
 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Fever, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain.
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): A new radiographic infiltrate with evidence of infection (fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis) with onset at least 48 hours after hospital admission.
 * 3.1.8 Nosocomial Pathogens (Klebsiella, Serratia, Pseudomonas) (3.1 Pneumonia): Pathogenesis: capsule (80 serotypes) impedes phagocytosis; endotoxin (fever, inflammation, shock); enzymes: cephalosporinases and ESBLs (resistance to cephalosporins).
 * 3.2.2 Pathogenesis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Symptoms None; bacilli dormant Malaise, low-grade fever, night sweats, fatigue, persistent cough, hemoptysis
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Systemic symptoms: weight loss, night sweats, malaise, fever
 * 3.2.6 Anti-TB Drugs (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): … (esp. slow acetylators; competition with pyridoxine); allergy (rash, fever, blood dyscrasias, hepatitis); hemolysis in G-6-PD deficiency. Inhibits metabolism of phenytoin

Chapter 5: Pleural effusion

 * 5.3 Chylothorax and Empyema: Typically the cavity is infected with anaerobic organisms; the patient is severely ill with high fever and neutrophil granulocytosis.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.5.1 Acute Empyema (7.5 Empyema of the Pleural Cavity): Marked dyspnea, fever, sweating and toxaemia.

Microbe Files (بطاقات الميكروبات)

 * Mycobacterium tuberculosis: أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) أعراض (symptoms) غير نوعية: توعك، إرهاق، تعرق ليلي، حمى (fever) خفيفة، نقص وزن. وفي العدوى التنفسية: سعال (cough) مستمر وبصاق دم (haemoptysis)
 * Mycoplasma pneumoniae: أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) حمى (fever)، صداع (headache)، سعال (cough) غير منتج
 * Chlamydia psittaci: اللقب: عدوى الببغاوات (Parrot fever)*
 * Klebsiella pneumoniae: …) الكبسولة (تعيق البلع وتساعد الالتصاق)؛ السم الداخلي Endotoxin (حمى (fever) والتهاب وصدمة إنتانية)؛ إنزيمات: cephalosporinases وESBL المسؤولة عن مقاومة (resistance) السيفالوسبورينات (c…
 * Influenza virus: أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) حمى (fever)، ألم عضلات، صداع (headache)، التهاب بلعوم (pharyngitis)، سعال (cough). وعادة لا يوجد سيلان أنف (coryza) الذي يميز نزلات البرد
 * Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV): أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) التهاب أنف وبلعوم مع حمى (fever)، قد يتبعه التهاب قصيبات والتهاب رئوي (pneumonia). لا فيروسيميا. السعال (cough) قد يستمر 3 أسابيع. وأغلب الحا…
 * Coronaviruses (SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2): …تقتل 3-30% من الحالات. وCOVID-19 يسبب مرضا يشبه الالتهاب الرئوي (حمى (fever)، صعوبة تنفس، سعال (cough) جاف، آفات منتشرة في الرئتين)
 * Aspergillus: …(symptoms)ا. وعدوى الرشاشيات الغازية السريعة تسبب سعال (cough)ا وحمى (fever) وألم صدر وصعوبة تنفس

title: Hemoptysis
content:
HEMOPTYSIS

سعال الدم

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

خروج دم أو بلغم مختلط بدم من الجهاز التنفسي السفلي بالسعال (coughing up blood).


الأسباب في المنهج (CAUSES)

 * السل (TB): خاصة مع التجاويف.
 * توسع القصبات: قد يكون غزيرا ومهددا للحياة لأنه من الشرايين القصبية عالية الضغط.
 * سرطان الرئة (bronchial carcinoma).
 * خراج الرئة (نزيف قد يكون غزيرا).
 * الاحتشاء الرئوي (pulmonary infarction).


تمييزه (DISTINGUISH)

يختلف عن القيء الدموي (hematemesis): الأول مع سعال وبلون أحمر زاهٍ ومختلط بهواء/بلغم.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Hemoptysis: bloodstained sputum or massive hemorrhage.
 * 1.3.4 Treatment and Complications (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Severe, massive, life-threatening hemoptysis: originates from the high-pressure systemic bronchial arteries; mortality 25%.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Cough with copious purulent sputum, recurrent hemoptysis.
 * 1.4.1 Definition, Pathophysiology and Presentation (1.4 Lung Abscess): Productive cough, hemoptysis

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.2.2 Pathogenesis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Symptoms None; bacilli dormant Malaise, low-grade fever, night sweats, fatigue, persistent cough, hemoptysis
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Hemoptysis: more common with cavitary disease; up to two-thirds are smear-positive. Usually small; massive hemoptysis is rare, most common after destruction of a lobe with bronchiectasis.

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.3 Clinical Features (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Hemoptysis.

Microbe Files (بطاقات الميكروبات)

 * Mycobacterium tuberculosis: أعراض الجريمة (Crime signs / symptoms) أعراض (symptoms) غير نوعية: توعك، إرهاق، تعرق ليلي، حمى (fever) خفيفة، نقص وزن. وفي العدوى التنفسية: سعال (cough) مستمر وبصاق دم (haemoptysis)

احتباس الهواء في الرئتين فيبدو الصدر منتفخا ويقل ثباته (trapped air making the chest over-expanded).


علاماته (SIGNS)

ضعف حركة الصدر، اختفاء كتمة القلب والكبد، حجاب منخفض ومسطح في الأشعة. يظهر في COPD وانتفاخ الرئة والربو الحاد.

 * 1.2.5 Clinical Features (1.2 COPD): Poor chest expansion; hyperinflated lungs; loss of normal cardiac and liver dullness.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Chest X-ray: often normal. In advanced cases: overinflation with low flattened diaphragms, sometimes large bullae.

title: Hypotension and shock
content:
HYPOTENSION AND SHOCK

التعريف | DEFINITION

نقص تروية الأعضاء بسبب هبوط الدورة الدموية (inadequate organ perfusion).


أنواعه هنا (TYPES)

 * نقص حجم الدم (hypovolemic): دم الجنب والنزف.
 * توتري: استرواح الصدر التوتري.
 * إنتاني (septic): العدوى الشديدة.


علاماته (SIGNS)

هبوط الضغط، برودة وتعرق، شحوب، تسرع قلب.


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.6 Acute Severe Asthma (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Bradycardia or hypotension.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.8 Nosocomial Pathogens (Klebsiella, Serratia, Pseudomonas) (3.1 Pneumonia): Pathogenesis: capsule (80 serotypes) impedes phagocytosis; endotoxin (fever, inflammation, shock); enzymes: cephalosporinases and ESBLs (resistance to cephalosporins).

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.1 Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures (7.2 Fracture Ribs): General examination: dyspnea; signs of shock (neurogenic, hypovolemic); search for associated injuries (head, abdomen, limbs).
 * 7.2.2 Flail Chest (7.2 Fracture Ribs): … cannot be created on the normal side, so venous return decreases and shock worsens, ending in circulatory failure.
 * 7.3 Hemothorax: General: rapid pulse, subnormal temperature, hypotension; sweating and coldness (hypovolemic shock); increasing pallor and cyanosis.
 * 7.4.2 Open Pneumothorax (Sucking Chest Wound) (7.4 Pneumothorax): Severe cardio-respiratory distress with shock, cyanosis and dyspnea results from: paradoxical respiration and mediastinal flutter.
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Bilateral lung collapse (total on the affected side, partial on the opposite side) and shock.

title: Hypoxemia and hypoxia
content:
HYPOXEMIA AND HYPOXIA

نقص الأكسجة

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)

انخفاض أكسجين الدم الشرياني (PaO2 < 8 kPa أو 60 mmHg) (low oxygen in arterial blood).

زرقة، تسرع تنفس، تسرع قلب، ارتباك. يُقاس بـ ABG وبمقياس التأكسج (pulse oximetry).

title: Pulsus paradoxus
content:
PULSUS PARADOXUS

النبض المتناقض

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

انخفاض ضغط الدم الانقباضي بأكثر من 10 mmHg أثناء الشهيق (a fall in systolic BP > 10 mmHg on inspiration).


الدلالة (SIGNIFICANCE)

علامة شدة في نوبة الربو الحادة، وكذلك في انصباب التامور.

title: Sputum (Expectoration)
content:
SPUTUM (EXPECTORATION)

البلغم

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

إفرازات تُطرد من القصبات والرئتين بالسعال (secretions coughed up from the lower airway).


أشكاله (TYPES)

 * مخاطي أبيض/شفاف (mucoid): التهاب الشعب المزمن، COPD.
 * قيحي أصفر أو أخضر (purulent): عدوى بكتيرية، تفاقم COPD، توسع القصبات.
 * كريه الرائحة (foul): خراج الرئة (جراثيم لاهوائية).
 * كاكي سميك غزير يتغير مع الوضعية: توسع القصبات.
 * دموي (blood-stained): انظر سعال الدم.


فائدة فحصه (WHY EXAMINE)

يُرسل للصبغات والزرع (Gram، ZN، culture) وللخلايا الخبيثة (cytology).


يظهر في | SEEN IN (من ملاحظات الكتاب)

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.7 Asthma in Brief and Viva Questions (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Exacerbations with fever and yellowish sputum.
 * 1.2.1 Definition and Risk Factors (1.2 COPD): …n of the bronchi, clinically defined as repeated attacks of cough and expectoration for more than 3 months per year for 2 successive years; may increase the frequency of total and severe exacer…
 * 1.2.5 Clinical Features (1.2 COPD): Most common symptoms: dyspnea, cough, sputum production, wheezing. Dyspnea on exertion progresses gradually over time.
 * 1.2.6 Diagnosis and Assessment (1.2 COPD): Consider COPD in any patient with progressive dyspnea, chronic cough or sputum production, with a history of exposure to risk factors.
 * 1.2.7 Management of COPD (1.2 COPD): Antibiotics: patients can be given a supply to start as soon as the sputum turns yellow or green.
 * 1.3.1 Definition and Etiology (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Clinically: cough with production of large amounts of sputum, and dilated, thickened bronchi seen on CT. It is one of the suppurative lung diseases.
 * 1.3.2 Pathology (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Once developed, it gives a symptom complex dominated by cough and expectoration of conspicuous amounts of purulent sputum.
 * 1.3.3 Clinical Features and Investigations (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Early: yellow or green sputum only after an infection.
 * 1.3.4 Treatment and Complications (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Antibiotics: if sputum remains yellow or green despite regular physiotherapy, or if lung function deteriorates despite bronchodilators.
 * 1.3.5 Bronchiectasis in Brief and Viva Questions (1.3 Bronchiectasis): Cough with copious purulent sputum, recurrent hemoptysis.
 * 1.4.1 Definition, Pathophysiology and Presentation (1.4 Lung Abscess): Foul sputum or purulent pleural fluid
 * 1.4.2 Diagnosis and Investigations (1.4 Lung Abscess): Microbiological culture, ideally before starting antibiotics. Also useful to exclude tuberculosis. Blood cultures; sputum or bronchoscopy specimen (BAL needed).
 * 1.4.3 Management and Complications (1.4 Lung Abscess): Physiotherapy for drainage is common, given the purulent sputum.

Chapter 3: Pulmonary infections

 * 3.1.1 Definition, Classification and Routes of Infection (3.1 Pneumonia): The IDSA defines pneumonia as a new lung infiltrate with other clinical evidence supporting infection: new fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis, and decline in oxygenation.
 * 3.1.2 Pathology of Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): …n Return toward normal Exudate enzymatically digested and resorbed or expectorated; basic alveolar structure intact. Pleural exudate may resolve or organize, leaving fibrous thickening or adhe…
 * 3.1.3 Typical Bacterial Pathogens (Pneumococcus and Haemophilus) (3.1 Pneumonia): Laboratory diagnosis (specimen: sputum):
 * 3.1.4 Atypical Pathogens (Mycoplasma, Legionella, Chlamydia) (3.1 Pneumonia): Culture: sputum or throat washings in special transport medium; "fried egg" colonies on serum-enriched agar after 3 weeks.
 * 3.1.6 Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) (3.1 Pneumonia): Fever, cough, sputum, shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain.
 * 3.1.7 Nosocomial Pneumonia (3.1 Pneumonia): A new radiographic infiltrate with evidence of infection (fever, purulent sputum, leukocytosis) with onset at least 48 hours after hospital admission.
 * 3.2.1 Epidemiology and Microbiology of M. tuberculosis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Resistant to: drying (especially in sputum, for long periods); acids (3% HCl, 6% H2SO4) and alkalis (4% NaOH), both used to decontaminate samples; dyes …
 * 3.2.3 Laboratory Diagnosis (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Pulmonary TB: 3 successive morning sputum samples; bronchoalveolar lavage or lung biopsy. In children or when sputum is not expectorated: gastric aspirate.
 * 3.2.4 Clinical Features and Investigations (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): Chronic cough with sputum is not always present, even with smear-positive sputum.
 * 3.2.6 Anti-TB Drugs (3.2 Pulmonary Tuberculosis): …mptoms; ataxia, confusion; red-orange discoloration of urine, saliva, sputum. Hepatic microsomal enzyme inducer: decreases effect of oral anticoagulants, oral contraceptives, digitoxin, …

Chapter 4: Tumours of the lung

 * 4.1.2 Pathology and Histological Types (4.1 Bronchial Carcinoma): Develops through squamous metaplasia → dysplasia → carcinoma; changes can be detected by cytology of sputum, bronchial lavage or brushings.

Microbe Files (بطاقات الميكروبات)

 * Streptococcus pneumoniae: طريقة الكشف (التحقيق) (Detection / lab diagnosis) العينة: البلغم (sputum). صبغة جرام (Gram stain) (تشخيصية). Latex agglutination لكشف سكر المحفظة (capsule). الزرع (culture) على آجار …
 * Haemophilus influenzae: الشكل (Morphology / shape) عصيات (bacilli) صغيرة رفيعة؛ والسلالات غير المحفظية المعزولة من البلغم (sputum) متعددة الأشكال (pleomorphic)
 * Mycobacterium tuberculosis: مقاومة للـ (Resistant to) الجفاف (خاصة في البلغم (sputum))، الأحماض (3% HCl و6% H2SO4) والقلويات (4% NaOH)، الأصباغ (malachite green)، بعض المضادات (البنسلين (penicillin))، الظلام

title: Tracheal deviation - Mediastinal shift
content:
TRACHEAL DEVIATION / MEDIASTINAL SHIFT

انحراف القصبة / انزياح المنصف

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

انحراف القصبة الهوائية والمنصف (القلب) عن الوضع الطبيعي (trachea and mediastinum pushed or pulled).


القاعدة (RULE)

 * تُدفع بعيدا عن الجانب المصاب: انصباب جنب كبير، دم جنب، استرواح توتري (tension pneumothorax).
 * تُسحب نحو الجانب المصاب: انخماص (collapse) أو تليف.
 * يبقى في الوسط: استرواح بسيط أو انصباب صغير.

Chapter 5: Pleural effusion

 * 5.1 Clinical Picture and Radiology: Large effusions displace the mediastinum to the opposite side, unless there is underlying pulmonary collapse or pleural fibrosis.

Chapter 7: Thoracic surgery

 * 7.2.1 Aetiology and Simple Rib Fractures (7.2 Fracture Ribs): Palpation Localized tenderness and crepitus at the fracture; normal TVF in uncomplicated cases; no tracheal shift
 * 7.3 Hemothorax: Palpation: trachea deviated to the opposite side (mediastinal shift); decreased TVF.
 * 7.4.1 Aetiology and Closed (Simple) Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): Tracheal shift to the opposite side
 * 7.4.3 Tension Pneumothorax (7.4 Pneumothorax): …ansion; marked decrease in respiratory movement on the affected side; tracheal shift to the opposite side; hyper-resonance; decreased TVF and decreased breath sounds.

title: Wheeze
content:
WHEEZE

الصفير

النوع (Type): عرض أو علامة (Symptom / sign)


التعريف | DEFINITION

صوت موسيقي عالي النغمة يُسمع غالبا في الزفير، سببه مرور الهواء في قصبات ضيقة (a high-pitched musical sound from narrowed airways).


متى يُسمع (WHEN)

الربو (منتشر ومتقلب)، COPD، التهاب القصبات، انسداد موضعي بورم أو جسم غريب (يكون موضعيا).


تنبيه (CAUTION)

غيابه مع شدة ضيق النفس = «صدر صامت» (silent chest) وهو علامة خطيرة.

Chapter 1: Airway diseases

 * 1.1.1 Definition and Classification (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): …imitation and inflammation of the bronchi, causing symptoms of cough, wheeze, chest tightness and dyspnea.
 * 1.1.4 Clinical Presentation and Investigations (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Recurrent episodes of cough and wheeze after exposure to an airborne allergen or pollutant; symptoms vary in time and in intensity.
 * 1.1.7 Asthma in Brief and Viva Questions (1.1 Bronchial Asthma): Is there reversible airway obstruction? Are the wheezing and breathlessness reversible?
 * 1.2.5 Clinical Features (1.2 COPD): Most common symptoms: dyspnea, cough, sputum production, wheezing. Dyspnea on exertion progresses gradually over time.
